The Singapore Police Force (SPF) plays a critical role in keeping Singapore safe and secure with our mission to prevent, deter and detect crime.

The key functions of CPS are Infrastructure Protection Regulation, Capability Development and Protective Engineering. In addition, CPS collaborates with various public and private stakeholders to reinforce the IPA and synergize efforts to improve the security industry.

You will be working in a fast-paced and highly volatile environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time.","Crime Scene Response and Management — Attend and support the management of crime scenes, incident scenes and other scenes of forensic interest. Governance, Quality and Readiness — Ensure crime scene processes comply with established procedures, safety requirements, legal considerations and evidential standards. You will maintain readiness of crime scene equipment and operational resources, support audits and quality assurance activities, and keep abreast of developments in forensic science and crime scene investigation methods.","We are looking for candidates who are operationally grounded, meticulous and committed to supporting investigations through sound forensic practice.

The Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB), a government agency under the Ministry of Trade and Industry, is responsible for strategies that enhance Singapore’s position as a global centre for business, innovation, and talent. About the Environmental Sustainability Division

The Environmental Sustainability division in EDB charts the vision and strategy for Singapore to transit to a low-carbon economy and leverage environmental sustainability trends as a growth engine. We also develop and execute national and ecosystem-level strategies to improve Singapore’s competitiveness in energy, chemicals and materials, and identify new green growth opportunities in established and emerging industries. To achieve this mission, we undertake research, analysis and solutions development in close partnership with others teams in EDB, as well as external stakeholders in government and industry.

This is primarily an individual contributor role. With guidance from the Vice President / Assistant Vice President, you will contribute to the development of new sustainable growth sectors such as the Bioeconomy for Singapore, in the following manner:

You will make rapid assessments of emerging opportunities to determine which would be suitable for support.

  • Sense and analyse: You will conduct in-depth industry studies to uncover emerging green growth opportunities for Singapore. This includes analysing market size and growth potential, mapping value chains, assessing the strength of Singapore's existing ecosystem to support new opportunities, and evaluating Singapore's competitive positioning and right to win. You will structure complex industries and distill insights in a clear and compelling manner for senior stakeholders and decision-makers.

  • Develop and execute: You will recommend specific interventions and strategies for how Singapore can best position itself to win in identified green growth sectors such as the Bioeconomy. This includes working closely with teams across EDB and relevant government agencies to design value propositions, and coordinate approaches to sector development. You will also engage with companies, both established players and emerging innovators to gather market intelligence and conduct initial investment promotion activities.

  • Stakeholder management: You will work independently to navigate across multiple internal and external stakeholders, building relationships with government agency partners and industry players to gather insights, align on priorities, and drive execution of Bioeconomy initiatives. As a Senior Manager/ Manager in Youth Engagement and Research, you will:

","

  • Conduct qualitative and quantitative research to understand perceptions, motivations, challenges, and behaviours of youths pertaining to work and career planning
  • Identify and explore emerging youths-related trends in education, employment, values and identity, and how these impact school-to-work transitions and early career decisions and pathways
  • Synthesize research insights into actionable recommendations to inform programmes, partnerships, and outreach strategies
  • Support internal teams with youth-related insights and frameworks to ensure initiatives are designed with empathy and relevance
  • Engage with youth-focused organisations, educators, community groups, and ecosystem partners to develop collaborative initiatives and expand outreach
  • Cultivate and maintain strong partnerships with youth organisations, education institutions and community stakeholders to co-develop impactful initiatives
  • Design and lead youth-centric pilot initiatives and engagements to test new approaches to career development and planning, including both digital and in-person formats
  • Develop funding proposals, grant applications and programme budgets for youth-related initiatives and pilots
  • Manage and monitor grants and programme funding for assigned initiatives, ensuring compliance with funding requirements, proper governance, and effective utilisation of resources
  • Work closely with internal stakeholders to ensure timely funding disbursement, tracking and reporting of programme outcomes
  • Track and evaluate the outcomes and effectiveness of youth-related initiatives and surface insights for broader implementation
  • Present insights and recommendations clearly and persuasively to internal and external stakeholders, including senior management and external partners

","

  • Relevant experience in youth engagement, market and consumer/user research, programme development, community development and/or grants/funding management
  • Strong grasp of qualitative and/or quantitative research methods, including survey design, interviews, focus groups, or user testing
  • Familiarity with trends in youth development, education-to-work transitions, and socio-economic issues affecting young people
  • Experience working with or designing initiatives for diverse youth profiles, including students, graduates, and early-career workers
  • Proficient in MS Office, especially PowerPoint and Excel; familiarity with data visualisation or research tools is a plus

You should possess the following skill sets:

  • Youth Empathy and Engagement: Able to relate to and connect with diverse youth mindsets; comfortable designing programmes or touchpoints that resonate with their needs and realities
  • Research and Insight Development: Skilled in gathering, analysing and interpreting data to surface insights that shape programmes and strategies

The Prudential Policy Department (PPD) fosters a sound and dynamic financial sector through prudential policy formulation.

,"

Within PPD, the Prudential Advisory Division (PAD) formulates deposit insurance policies that support the orderly resolution of failing banks, with the aim of maintaining financial stability and protecting small depositors. You will help ensure that the deposit insurance framework strikes the right balance across competing policy considerations, and that its implementation processes run smoothly.

We also work with colleagues across PPD to design and implement the capital framework for banks, focusing on the eligibility of capital instruments (such as Additional Tier 1 instruments) and disclosure requirements. This work is grounded in the international Basel III regulatory framework and spans research and analysis, drafting legislative amendments, and engaging with banks on regulatory queries.

Beyond domestic policy work, we support senior management's participation in international fora — principally the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and the Financial Stability Board. In this capacity, you will contribute to international policymaking on banking prudential issues and broader financial stability risks, while advocating for Singapore's interests. Work at these fora may touch on emerging or cross-cutting issues that do not fall neatly within any single department's remit. As the home of banking prudential policy in MAS, PAD takes the lead in coordinating and advancing Singapore's positions on such issues. Through this work, you will deepen your understanding of international dynamics and emerging risks, and how regulation is used to address them, while building close working relationships with colleagues across MAS. The role will also sharpen your writing, analytical, and interpersonal skills.

Successful candidates will be assigned a portfolio covering a subset of these responsibilities.

","

  • Have the ability to persuade stakeholders with entrenched views, and the resilience to revisit and refine positions through multiple rounds of feedback, while remaining open to pivoting as facts and circumstances evolve.

  • Enjoy working as part of a team — proactively seeking inputs from others, surfacing interactions between different workstreams, and navigating differences in opinion constructively.

  • Be self-directed learners who can identify gaps in their own knowledge and skills, and take initiative to develop themselves professionally.

The following would be an advantage:

  • A keen interest in Basel III, banking crisis management, international policy dynamics, and emerging issues in the financial and regulatory space.

  • A healthy scepticism and ability to stress-test assumptions - particularly useful when imagining adverse scenarios to craft robust deposit insurance policies.

  • An enjoyment of coordination work, stakeholder engagement, and staying current on banking regulatory and supervisory developments.

c)
column4:

PRINCIPAL / SENIOR / EXECUTIVE ENGINEER

We are seeking a passionate and experienced Solution Architect to play a key role in the modernisation of Singapore’s Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) system, which supports Account-Based Ticketing & Card-Based Ticketing, to deliver seamless, secure, and scalable public transport experience. This is a high-impact opportunity to contribute to the digital transformation of Singapore's public transport infrastructure and help shape solutions that are seamless, secure, and built to scale.

As part of the System Architecture and Assurance Division, you will lead end-to-end solution design, architecture governance, and technical assessments across a complex landscape of payment systems, cloud services, and multi-vendor integrations — ensuring reliability and security at a national scale.

What You Will Do

  • Architect secure, scalable, and high-availability solutions for AFC and payment systems, including those built on EMV, open-loop standards, account-based ticketing, and card-based ticketing models in the GCC2.0 AWS environment.

  • Design and govern end-to-end system integration architectures across distributed, multi-vendor environments, leveraging event-driven patterns and message-oriented middleware including messaging protocols such as MQ and MQTT, communication protocols such as HTTP/S and WebSockets, and integration patterns such as REST APIs, webhooks, and pub/sub architectures, to support both real-time and asynchronous processing needs.

  • Lead security architecture design to ensure compliance with Govtech’s IM8 and security requirements to safeguard sensitive payment and commuter data.

  • Lead network infrastructure design, including the planning and governance of network topology, connectivity, and security controls across cloud and hybrid environments to ensure scalable, resilient, and secure deployments

  • Produce and maintain system architecture and networking infrastructure diagrams, API and interface specifications, and integration designs with clear documentation of network infrastructure components.

  • Translate business and system requirements into high-level and detailed technical specifications, interface designs, and integration patterns suited to complex multi-system environments. Perform technical impact analysis for change requests and system enhancements, ensuring minimal disruption to mission-critical AFC operations.

  • Conduct solution walkthroughs, architecture reviews, and technical presentations for internal and external stakeholders. Collaborate with internal stakeholders (project teams, software development, operations) and external partners (vendors, financial institutions) to develop robust and future-ready solutions.

","

  • Knowledge in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, or related field.

  • At least 5 years of experience in solution architecture, systems analysis/design, or complex enterprise IT infrastructure.

  • Networks and Protocols — working knowledge of common network and communication protocols such as TCP/IP, HTTP/S, FTPS, and SFTP, and the OSI model as applied to enterprise system design.

  • Enterprise Integration Patterns — experience designing solutions using APIs, webhooks, WebSockets, message queues, MQTT, and pub/sub or event-driven architectures across complex, multi-system environments.

  • Data and Interfaces — familiarity with data serialisation formats such as JSON and binary, and how these are applied across system integration touchpoints.

  • Network Infrastructure — understanding of IP addressing, CIDR, subnets, firewalls, routers, MPLS, and availability zone design in cloud and hybrid environments.

​Bonus Skills:

  • AWS certifications (e.g., AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate/Professional) are strongly preferred

  • Experience in Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) systems, open-loop payment architecture, or financial-grade transaction systems.

  • Strong knowledge of security architecture, including secure data flows, tokenisation, encryption, and compliance standards (e.g., PCI DSS).

  • Hands-on exposure to DevSecOps, CI/CD, containerisation (e.g., ECS, EKS), serverless architecture, or data streaming pipelines.

  • Security and Compliance — experience embedding a defence-in-depth approach across all layers of solution design, encompassing network security, identity and access management, data protection, encryption, vulnerability management, and threat detection and response, with a strong understanding of government and industry compliance standards such as IM8 and PCI-DSS.

  • GCC AWS — familiarity with Singapore's Government Commercial Cloud on AWS, including its governance requirements and deployment constraints.

",Others,Full-time

hrp,005056a3-d347-1fe1-9daa-0b783a8462ad,17779895,Manager (Industrial Security Research),Military Security Department,0000009180,"The Military Security Department (MSD)’s core business is in Counter Intelligence and internal security for MINDEF/SAF. ","

The Climate Change in Southeast Asia Programme (CCSEAP) at the ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute was established in 2020 to examine the phenomenon of climate change, its impact, and policy responses across the region. Building on ISEAS’ thought leadership, the programme seeks to advance climate discourse and knowledge in Southeast Asia through research, policy papers, publications, seminars and workshops. Applications are invited for:

Senior Fellow (Energy/Climate) & Co-Coordinator, CCSEAP (2-year contract)

","

The Senior Fellow’s primary focus of research is on Southeast Asia’s energy transitions in the context of a green recovery and the nexus between energy and climate. The Senior Fellow will examine the political, economic, social, technological and/or policy implications of these interactions in the context of planned energy transitions in the region. Country expertise and focus on selected Southeast Asian countries will be an advantage.

As Co-Coordinator, the candidate is also expected to bring a broader view across the programme’s wider climate agenda — including climate diplomacy, ASEAN climate governance, and adaptation — sufficient to help set direction for the programme, and not solely their own individual research project. Secondary research focus may be on, but is not limited to, carbon pricing, carbon markets, labour transition issues, green technology or sustainable finance.

Job Responsibilities

  • Conduct research and provide analysis, and co-lead the programme’s overall research agenda and strategic priorities together with the Coordinator, including the allocation of work among researchers and Research Officers

  • Contribute regularly to ISEAS’ research products such as Fulcrum commentary, ISEAS Perspective, and Trends in Southeast Asia;

  • Take primary responsibility for specific external grants, including donor reporting, budget tracking, and management of stakeholder expectations;

  • Co-lead the conceptualisation, execution and analysis of the Southeast Asia Climate Outlook Survey;

  • Build and maintain the programme's external network — including with the ASEAN Secretariat, regional think-tank networks, multilateral bodies, government counterparts and donors — representing the programme externally and deputising for the Coordinator when required

  • Plan, organise and take lead responsibility for seminars, workshops and outreach activities in accordance with the Institute’s mission;

  • Supervise and mentor junior researchers, Research Officers and interns within the programme;

  • Identify and help cultivate new funding opportunities and donor relationships for the programme;

  • Contribute to the programme’s multi-year strategic planning in alignment with ISEAS’ institutional priorities;

  • Serve as an internal reviewer/editor for Programme publications to help maintain quality and consistency

","

Job Requirements

  • A PhD degree in Climate Science, Climate Policy, Environmental Policy, Energy, Public Policy, International Relations, or a related discipline;

  • At least 8–15 years of relevant research and/or policy experience, including demonstrated experience in programme or project management, team leadership, or grant/fund management;

  • A strong, established track record of publications and thought leadership in the climate–energy nexus (peer-reviewed and policy outputs, media presence, invited talks);

  • Demonstrated experience managing budgets, donor relationships, or research teams;

  • An existing network within the regional and/or international climate-energy policy community (e.g. ASEAN bodies, multilateral institutions, donor agencies) will be an advantage;

  • Strong interdisciplinary orientation and interest in the nexus between climate change and energy;

  • Excellent communication and writing skills in English; working knowledge of other Southeast Asian languages will be an advantage;

  • Awareness of regional and global developments, and ability to contribute to the strategic and policy-oriented direction of research projects aligned with ISEAS's mandate.

  • Ability to lead and manage research projects, including planning, resource management and securing research funding.

  • Team player with strong leadership, mentoring, interpersonal and networking skills, and diplomatic skill in managing stakeholders and donors;

  • Willingness to be based full-time in Singapore for the duration of the appointment.

Applications should include a cover letter, a full CV, three referee contacts (including at least one who can speak to the candidate’s managerial or leadership experience), a strong research proposal on energy transitions in Southeast Asia of not more than five pages (double spaced), a one-page statement of vision for the programme’s strategic priorities and stakeholder/donor management over the appointment period, and a writing sample of a commentary nature.

The research proposal should discuss the topic to be examined, plans for any fieldwork and duration, projected timeline of research, and output.

Opportunities for renewal will be considered, subject to performance and funding.

Remuneration and benefits will depend on the candidate’s qualifications and experience.

",Others,Full-time

The officer will play a key role in operationalising SLA's AI governance framework, administering governance processes, and ensuring AI initiatives comply with Whole-of-Government requirements while enabling innovation and business value.

Policy Development & Compliance

  • Develop and maintain AI governance policies, SOPs, templates and guidance materials.
  • Monitor emerging AI governance developments and assess implications for SLA.
  • Maintain AI governance records, inventories and management reporting.

  • Experience supporting governance committees, review boards or risk management functions.
  • Familiarity with Generative AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), Machine Learning and emerging AI technologies.
  • Knowledge of data governance, cybersecurity, privacy and information management practices.
  • Experience working within the Singapore Public Service or Whole-of-Government digital transformation initiatives.

Personal Attributes

  • Strong analytical thinking and sound judgement.
  • Meticulous and detail-oriented with a structured approach to governance and compliance matters.
  • Strong interpersonal and stakeholder management skills.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-evolving technology environment.

","

  • Good understanding of labour market, workforce transformation trends, including the impact of technology and automation.

  • Proactive, with a strong sense of ownership and follow-through.

The Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) is Singapore’s land use planning and conservation authority. Our mission is to make Singapore a great city to live, work and play. We plan and facilitate the physical development of Singapore, in partnership with agencies and the community, to create a vibrant, sustainable and cosmopolitan city of distinction.
About URBEX and DPLab

URA has spearheaded efforts to strengthen urban planning and design workflows through the application of urban science, geospatial and data analytics, modelling and simulation (M&S), and AI technologies. In 2022, URA was designated as the Whole-of-Government (WOG) Urban Planning & Design Technology Centre of Excellence (URBEX), to lead the planning and design sector in building up these strategic capabilities.

The Design & Planning Lab (DPLab) is a multi-disciplinary team in URA which drives URBEX efforts. In recognition of our work, URA was conferred the 2024 Esri Special Achievement in Geographic Information System (GIS) Award for demonstrating vision, leadership and innovation in the use of GIS technology. URA was also awarded the Esri Singapore GeoInnovation Award in 2024 for being amongst Singapore’s most progressive organisations in the use of geospatial solutions to transform the future. Our flagship product, ePlanner (a web-based geospatial platform that brings digital planning tools to WOG) also won the Excellence Award at the Singapore Public Service’s Science, Technology and Engineering Conference 2024.

In DPLab, you will work alongside talented individuals with expertise in wide-ranging domains including data policy, governance, strategy and engineering, product strategy, business analysis, software engineering, cloud engineering, urban design technologies, data science, AI/Machine Learning, and M&S.  You will also work closely with planners, architects, and policymakers to co-create digital solutions that contribute to enhancing the liveability, sustainability and resilience of our city-state.","As a Data Scientist (Computational Design), you will help build parametric systems that generate, analyse, and evaluate building and urban form — from individual building massing to neighbourhood and city-scale scenarios. column1: hrp,005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a3e0-7fc7043ab402,17905813,Customs Officer,Singapore Customs,0000001182,"Singapore Customs is a government agency under the Ministry of Finance. Singapore Customs advances Singapore’s economic development by protecting revenue and facilitating trade for a thriving Singapore economy. You can look forward to seamless advancement opportunities with our integrated grade structure under the Customs Unified Scheme of Service (CUS).","In Singapore Customs, we work, play, learn and grow together as OneCustoms team. With regular job rotations under our Open Posting System that offer many opportunities for competency and skills development, you will get to experience our Customs core functions in trade facilitation, regulation and compliance as well as enforcement during the foundational phase.

· Law Enforcer: You protect Singapore’s revenue by adopting a whole-of-government approach, and working closely with other enforcement agencies to enforce against revenue-related and trade offences.

column1: hrp,005056a3-d347-1fe1-a492-a180fff062ad,17889333,Asst Director/Snr Asst Director/Deputy Director (Medical Service Scheme),Ministry of Health,0000001200,"The Ministry of Health’s (MOH) vision is to champion a healthy nation with our people – to live well, live long and with peace of mind. MOH constantly grapples with new challenges brought on by an increasingly globalised world, a rapidly ageing population and rising expectations. Programme and Content

As part of the National Archives of Singapore (NAS), the Digital Preservation Team is responsible for managing the transfer, preservation, and access of government records of archival value. As an archivist in the Digital Preservation Team, you will play a hands-on role across system development and maintenance, workflow design, and policy and guidelines development, working closely with technical and non-technical stakeholders. A typical week might involve writing a Python script to automate a manual task, meeting with government agencies to walk them through transfer requirements or clarifying their queries, working with IT and vendors on system enhancements or issues, and exploring a new tool to assess whether it could support digital preservation workflows. This is neither a pure IT role nor a traditional archival role — there will be both technical or generalist tasks, as well as stakeholder engagement.

Location: National Archives of Singapore, 1 Canning Rise, Singapore 179868
Division/Dept: National Archives / Records Management (RM) - Digital Preservation

","

Systems and Technologies:

• Act as the business user representative in the development, maintenance, and enhancement of multiple digital systems and platforms, working with users, IT colleagues and vendors on requirements gathering, user acceptance testing, issue resolution, and management of project timelines and budget.

• Review and maintain systems documentation such as Requirements Specifications, User Manuals, and Test Scripts.

• Monitor system performance and troubleshoot issues to facilitate the transfer, ingestion and preservation of digital records.

• Write scripts in Python or other scripting languages to automate repetitive tasks and improve work processes.

• Work with IT colleagues to review and improve workflows across the full records management lifecycle — including appraisal, transfer, preservation, and access — identifying opportunities for automation or process enhancement.

Digital Recordkeeping and Preservation:

• Prepare and ingest legacy digitised records into systems, including identifying and resolving data quality issues to ensure records meet ingestion requirements.

• Collaborate with government agencies to facilitate the seamless transfer and ingestion of records to NAS, providing clear guidance on transfer requirements and resolving issues that arise throughout the process.

• Maintain and update various documentation (e.g. policies, guidelines, and specifications) related to digital recordkeeping and preservation.

• Experiment with and evaluate tools and technologies for digital preservation — including established tools (e.g. SIARD, Bagger) and emerging technologies such as Generative AI — developing Proof of Concepts and scaling up successful pilots into regular workflows.

• Monitor developments across diverse digital record formats and platforms (e.g. emails, databases, collaboration tools such as MS Teams), and propose guidelines or approaches for how NAS should handle these, including identifying and evaluating relevant tools where applicable.

Engagement and Advocacy:

• Regularly engage government agencies to facilitate the transfer of records to NAS, including troubleshooting issues, coordinating logistics, and providing training and guidance on NAS's transfer requirements, policies, and guidelines.

• Engage internal and external stakeholders on collaborative projects relating to digital preservation and archiving.

","

column1: hrp,005056a3-d347-1fe1-a495-2f488b3d62ad,17914072,Finance Compliance Officer,MHA - Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF),0000001086,"The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. An operationally ready SCDF, working hand-in-hand with a prepared and resilient population, helps to ensure that the nation is capable of handling any untoward eventualities.",1785888000000,1787097600000,Closing in 3 day(s),1  week(s) ago,Permanent,0001,02-05 year(s),2,5,Accounting & Finance,0001,Accounting & Finance,0001,"Accounting, Audit, Finance",03,false,,"This role is part of MHA’s Civilian Generalist career track. This is a 2-year position as a Senior Lecturer, Inclusive Education & Learning Support in the School of Humanities & Interdisciplinary Studies.

We are seeking an experienced and passionate educator with deep expertise in special educational needs (SEN), inclusive education and learning support to lead the School's efforts in developing inclusive teaching and assessment practices. The role requires someone who can work confidently across a broad spectrum of learning disabilities and neurodevelopmental conditions, and who can guide academic staff in making evidence-based accommodations within the Polytechnic's academic and assessment frameworks.

In this role, you will serve as the School's key specialist resource for inclusive education, partnering with lecturers, course teams, student support professionals and academic leaders to support complex student cases, build staff capability and establish effective practices that balance student support with academic standards.

In addition to leading the School's inclusive education initiatives, you will contribute to teaching and curriculum development within the Diploma in Psychology & Community Development (PCD), as well as support the growth of Continuing Education and Training (CET) offerings in areas related to disability inclusion, special educational needs and learning support. This is a unique opportunity to shape inclusive educational practices at scale while making a meaningful impact on student success across the Polytechnic.

","

Your responsibilities will include, but are not limited to, the following:

Inclusive Learning and Assessment Support

  • Advise academic staff on appropriate teaching, learning and assessment accommodations for students with special educational needs while ensuring alignment with Ngee Ann Polytechnic's academic and assessment frameworks.

  • Review and provide recommendations on complex student cases involving a wide range of learning disabilities, neurodevelopmental conditions and learning differences.

  • Partner lecturers and course teams to implement reasonable accommodations that support student success without compromising learning outcomes or assessment integrity.

  • Develop practical resources, guidelines and frameworks to strengthen inclusive teaching and assessment practices across the School.

  • Support the School's efforts to build a more inclusive learning environment through evidence-based and sustainable practices.

Capability Development and Staff Training

  • Design and deliver professional development programmes for academic staff on inclusive education, universal design for learning, differentiated instruction and assessment accommodations.

  • Build staff confidence and capability in supporting students with diverse learning needs across classroom, project-based and assessment settings.

  • Curate and share emerging practices, research and evidence-based approaches in inclusive education and learning support.

  • Lead school-wide initiatives and projects relating to learner diversity, accessibility and inclusion.

Student Support and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Work closely with student support professionals, academic leaders and relevant stakeholders to coordinate support strategies for students with learning needs.

  • Provide consultation and case management support for students requiring significant accommodations or intervention.

  • Partner internal and external stakeholders to strengthen support systems and referral pathways for students requiring specialised assistance.

Teaching and Academic Contributions

  • Undertake curriculum development, teaching and student supervision duties within the Diploma in Psychology & Community Development (PCD).

  • Deliver modules in areas related to psychology, disability inclusion, special educational needs, community development, helping professions and related disciplines, depending on expertise and School needs.

  • Design, develop and facilitate Continuing Education and Training (CET) programmes for adult learners and industry professionals in areas relating to disability inclusion, supporting individuals with special educational needs, inclusive practices and related topics.

  • Contribute to the development of new PET and CET offerings that strengthen professional capabilities in inclusive education, disability support and community inclusion.

  • Participate in School initiatives, projects and committees that support educational excellence and student success.

","

  • Relevant qualifications in Education, Special Education, Psychology, Educational Psychology, Learning Support or a related discipline. Postgraduate qualifications will be an advantage.

  • Significant professional experience supporting individuals with a broad spectrum of learning disabilities, neurodevelopmental conditions and learning differences, including but not limited to autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, dyslexia and less commonly encountered learning disabilities.

  • Demonstrated experience teaching in a mainstream educational institution, with a strong understanding of the opportunities and challenges of inclusive classroom practice.

  • Strong understanding of assessment accommodations and the ability to recommend and implement support measures that maintain academic standards and assessment integrity.

  • Experience advising, coaching or training educators in inclusive education, learning support or related areas.

  • Strong facilitation, consultation and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to work effectively with academic staff, student support professionals and leadership teams.

  • Experience designing and delivering adult learning, professional development or CET programmes will be an advantage.

  • Knowledge of universal design for learning, differentiated instruction, accessibility and evidence-based intervention strategies.

  • A collaborative, empathetic and solutions-oriented mindset, coupled with sound professional judgement when managing complex cases involving students with diverse learning needs.

Successful candidates should possess both deep expertise in inclusive education and the ability to operate effectively within a mainstream educational environment, supporting staff and students while balancing inclusion, academic standards and institutional requirements

You will be part of the Risk Assurance Division within IMDA’s Resilience and Cybersecurity Group. The Holistic Assessment team in this Division assesses the overall cybersecurity risk posture of critical digital networks and systems and the cyber capabilities of organisations operating these networks.

This includes integrating diverse sources of information, across the organisation’s external environment, its internal capabilities and the performance of its networks and systems. The team adopts an evidence-based approach to develop an objective assessment of the organisation and network’s key strengths and vulnerabilities. It also recommends key areas that senior management should track to uplift its cybersecurity risk posture.

The Holistic Assessment team works with teams across IMDA’s Resilience and Cybersecurity Group, and in partnership with industry stakeholders. It regularly engages senior management in both IMDA and the industry, to review its findings and recommendations. Through these, the Holistic Assessment team plays a critical role in ensuring that the critical digital networks and systems which underpin Singapore’s Digital Economy remain secure and resilient.

","

  • Conduct research and sense making of the evolving cybersecurity landscape in relation to Singapore’s digital infrastructure. This includes integrating threat intelligence information as well as international industry best practices for defending against current and emerging cyber threats.
  • Review and assess key priorities that inspections should focus on, based on the current and emerging threat landscape, as well as potential vulnerabilities surfaced in cyber audit reports and remediations implemented.
  • Design technical tests to validate the effectiveness of cybersecurity measures within these priority areas. This requires a deep understanding of the network design, what the cybersecurity measures are intended to protect against, as well as how they contribute to the overall cybersecurity of the digital network and systems as a whole.
  • Conduct the technical validation tests.
  • Synthesise key findings from the inspections, on the strengths and vulnerabilities of the network. Recommend remediations that should be implemented to improve the overall cybersecurity of the digital network and systems inspected.

The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) is Singapore's central bank and integrated financial regulator. MEPS+ (Central Banking & Devt Platforms Division) is responsible for the MAS Electronic Payment System — a mission-critical system supporting interbank payments, government securities management, and domestic market infrastructure. MEPS+ serves the entire Singapore financial sector and requires 24/7 operational reliability, strict compliance with government regulatory frameworks, and close coordination with financial institutions and government agencies.

As System Manager, you are the operational and delivery owner for MEPS+ and related systems. You own the outcomes, and coordinate across software engineers, product owners, compliance teams, and external vendors to ensure system reliability, regulatory compliance, and successful delivery of enhancements and patches.

","

Operational Delivery & Application Portfolio Management

  • Own operational delivery outcomes for the MEPS+ application portfolio across interbank payments, government securities management, and domestic market infrastructures. Make and recommend strategic decisions on application rationalisation, consolidation, or decommissioning to optimise portfolio efficiency.

  • Coordinate release management and delivery cycles with product owners, ensuring timely and quality deployment of enhancements, patches, and security updates across major (semi-annual) and monthly patch cycles.

  • Own Service Level Objectives (SLOs) for applications under management. Review SLI and SLO performance reports produced by the SRE team, identify trends and deviations, and escalate or drive remediation as appropriate. Set requirements for monitoring coverage and alert quality; hold the SRE team accountable for outcomes.

  • Coordinate verification of monthly and quarterly system patching with the SRE team. Ensure patch outcomes are documented and meet compliance requirements.

Tech Delivery Manager Responsibilities (During Release Cycles)

  • Lead release planning and delivery activities during major enhancement releases (semi-annual). Coordinate with product owners, development teams, testing teams, and vendors to establish release scope, timelines, and deployment readiness criteria.

  • Manage release communication to all stakeholders. Provide status updates, escalate blockers, and maintain stakeholder alignment on release objectives and timelines throughout the cycle.

  • Own release governance and quality standards for MEPS+. Define the release readiness criteria and test governance framework that the Software Engineer executes against. Review and sign off on test outcomes, patch verification results, and release readiness reports before production deployment.

Incident Management

  • Own the incident management framework for MEPS+. Define and maintain incident escalation paths, SLO targets (P1, P2, P3), and communication protocols. During major incidents, lead stakeholder communication and coordinate the response — software engineers provide technical investigation and resolution support.

  • Drive root cause analysis and post-mortems following significant incidents. Own the documentation of lessons learned and track implementation of preventive measures to reduce recurrence.

Vendor Coordination & Procurement

  • Own vendor governance for outsourced components and services. Chair vendor performance reviews, monitor SLA compliance, and make escalation decisions when vendor performance falls short. Coordinate with software engineers for detailed technical review of vendor-delivered code and fixes.

  • Lead MAS's participation in procurement activities for outsourced services, including defining tender specifications, evaluating vendor proposals, and contributing to contract negotiations.

Compliance, Governance & Risk Management

  • Coordinate RFI responses across the team, ensuring accurate and timely submission of supporting documentation.

  • Plan and lead resiliency exercises including Disaster Recovery drills, manual contingency procedures, and CyberEx participation. Validate system failover and recovery capabilities. Maintain compliance with ICT Governance policies and standards specific to government financial infrastructure.

","

Essential Criteria

  • 8+ years of progressive experience in managing, operating, or delivering complex mission-critical systems. Minimum 3–4 years in a delivery management, operations management, or technical programme management role with clear accountability for system reliability or release outcomes. Experience with payment systems, securities settlement, or financial infrastructure is advantageous but not required.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead incident response at an organisational level — owning stakeholder communication, driving post-mortems, and implementing systemic improvements. Track record of managing high-stakes operational environments.

  • Proven experience managing vendor relationships, chairing performance reviews, and holding vendors accountable to SLAs. Experience contributing to procurement or contract management activities.

  • Strong experience coordinating release cycles across multiple teams — development, testing, operations, and compliance — with accountability for release readiness decisions.

  • Excellent communication skills. Able to explain technical risks, operational decisions, and compliance requirements clearly to senior leadership, business stakeholders, and regulators. Strong written communication for incident reports, post-mortems, audit RFI responses, and governance documentation.

  • Comfortable working across technical domains without requiring deep hands-on expertise in every platform. Able to engage credibly with software engineers and SRE colleagues, ask the right questions, and make informed decisions based on their input.

  • Proven ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams — incident response, release coordination, compliance activities, vendor management — without losing attention to detail or governance rigour.

Desirable Criteria

  • Familiarity with Java/J2EE application environments, Linux/RHEL systems, or SQL — sufficient to engage meaningfully with engineering teams and understand technical risk, without necessarily being a hands-on practitioner.

  • Experience with containerisation technologies (Docker, Kubernetes) or cloud platforms (OpenShift, OpenStack) at a conceptual or governance level.

  • Experience with CICD pipelines, release automation, and test management frameworks.

  • Familiarity with observability and monitoring platforms (e.g. Grafana, ELK stack) from an operational governance perspective.

  • Familiarity with government IT environments and regulatory compliance frameworks (CCoP, CSP, AGO, IM8).

  • Agile delivery experience and comfort collaborating with product teams and development teams.

  • Relevant certifications (e.g. ITIL, PMP, AWS Solutions Architect, or equivalent).

","

The Centre for Autonomous Mobility (CAM) leads Singapore’s national effort to deploy autonomous vehicles (AVs) safely and at scale. AVs will reshape how Singapore moves — across use cases spanning passenger cars, public buses and goods vehicles. In the Deployment Ops team, you take each AV deployment from plan to operating service – owning the programme schedule, driving delivery across workstreams, and managing the operators, developers, infrastructure stakeholders, to ensure AVs are deployed smoothly.

Responsibilities

Plan and manage each deployment programme

  • Work with operators and developers to evaluate, review and fine-tune service routes and concepts of operations.
  • Build and own the programme plan, schedule and milestones for each AV deployment, tracking progress against baseline and reporting status.
  • Identify risks, dependencies and bottleneck early, to develop mitigation plans to keep deployments on track.
  • Align deployment operational plans with longer-term AV deployment strategy and transport plans, so that AV services improve overall transport connectivity.

Drive deployment operations on the ground

  • Run deployments end to end — from planning through AV applications, vehicle approvals, testing and service launch — keeping multiple workstreams on tight timelines.
  • Work with industry and technology partners to resolve issues quickly and get vehicles tested and deployed on schedule.
  • Oversee operational readiness and develop standard operating procedures for the smooth running of AV services once launched – monitor performance, surface issues, manage incidents, and drive continuous improvement.

Coordinate across stakeholders

  • Bring together industry players, operators, government agencies and internal teams, aligning their requirements, securing their support, and resolving operational issues.
  • Partner with Corporate Communications, industry media teams and CAM’s Engagement team to align public announcements and high-signature events around key deployment milestones.

Communicate deployment progress to leadership

  • Prepare clear progress reports on deployment plans, and statuses for senior management, including distilling complex operational detail into clear recommendations.

","

  • Has a strong programme or project management track record — preferably at least 2 years planning and delivering medium-to-large-scale projects or programmes.
  • Organised and meticulous — comfortable owning detailed plans, tracking progress against baseline, and keeping many moving parts on schedule while working independently in a fast-paced environment.
  • Works well across stakeholders — listens, builds alignment across cross-functional teams and external partners, and drives to outcomes independently while having the right instincts to know when to escalate for decision-making.
  • Communicates clearly — writes and reports well, with an eye for detail.
  • Takes initiative and stays calm in ambiguity — AV deployment is new ground, so plans will change and you’ll help shape them.
  • Hands-on programme management and project planning.
  • Experience in operations management, contracts or vendor management.

The Programme Head will support the Senior Programme Head in driving community partnership development and programme development, ensuring successful execution across assigned regions whilst fostering strong relationships with Grassroots Organisations (GROs), Grassroots Leaders (GRLs), and local community stakeholders.   • Help track and monitor the engagement and mobilisation of People and local partners to ensure successful programme delivery.

Partnership Development & Stakeholder Engagement

Monitoring & Evaluation

  • Monitor programme performance, including participation and outcomes. Provide feedback to senior leaders on programme effectiveness and areas for improvement.

Stakeholder Support

  • Provide on-the-ground support to People and Local community stakeholders, ensuring they are equipped with the necessary tools and resources to implement programmes successfully.

","

The Legal Policy Group (LPG) in the Ministry of Law (MinLaw) plays a critical role in upholding the rule of law, advancing access to justice, and ensuring a sound and progressive legal framework for Singaporeans.
What the role is

Under LPG, officers at the Civil & Legislative Policy Division (CLPD) do not just review laws — we play an important role in helping to shape the future of legal policy and governance in Singapore. Our team has driven reforms that touch the lives of Singaporeans every day. Some recent initiatives include:

column2: Relief for victims of harassment: In 2021, we established the Protection from Harassment Court to give victims of harassment faster, more accessible and affordable relief through simplified court processes.

Modernisation of laws: In 2023, we modernised our laws through legislative reforms that make it possible for statutory declarations, oaths, affirmations, and notarisations to be done through electronic means.

Strengthening family therapeutic justice: The Maintenance Enforcement Process (MEP) was introduced in May 2023 under the Family Justice Reform Act to improve the enforcement of maintenance orders, deter non-payment, and improve access to justice for maintenance applicants through efficient enforcement procedures and sustainable outcomes. In 2025, the Maintenance Enforcement Division was established within the Insolvency and Public Trustee's Office to administer the MEP, with Maintenance Enforcement Officers working to achieve these objectives.

Enhancing the management of community disputes: In 2024, we worked closely with the MND and MCCY on enhancements to our Community Disputes Management Framework. The enhancements strengthen our community mediation framework and court processes to address neighbour disputes. Government agencies also worked together to introduce a Community Relations Unit that has powers to intervene in and address serious neighbour disputes.

Safer online spaces for Singaporeans: In November 2025, MinLaw and MDDI passed the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act. The Act strengthens online safety and protects Singaporeans from online harms. It empowers victims to seek timely relief and obtain redress through a new Online Safety Commission, and through new statutory torts that provide clear legal basis for victims of online harms to take action against those responsible for such harms.

column1: hrp,005056a3-d347-1fe1-a2df-fb07c98642ad,16923079,"Manager/Asst Director/Snr Asst Director, Community Relations Unit(Hoarding Mgmt)",Ministry of National Development,0000001140,"The Ministry of National Development (MND), the lead government agency responsible for land use planning and infrastructure development, aims to transform Singapore into an endearing home and a distinctive global city. The HMCG supports the New Environment Action Team (NEAT), an Alliance for Action intended to coordinate hoarding management efforts across the public, people and private (3P) sectors to address hoarding issues in a more holistic and sustainable manner.

In addition, the Community Relations Unit (CRU) in MSO is piloting a new concept of operations to tackle severe neighbour noise disputes and hoarding cases. These include cases where the severe hoarding has affected surrounding neighbours, and cases where the hoarding behaviour could be due to an underlying mental health condition.

Besides providing secretarial support to the HMCG and NEAT, your primary roles will be in case management and hoarding operations policy and planning.","Your key responsibilities would include the following:

column2: Managing and working towards the resolution of complex hoarding cases by gathering facts, assessing and triaging cases, and coordinating actions with stakeholders (e.g. partner agencies and NEAT community partners).

column1: You may also contribute to reviewing the pilot and shaping how this model could be improved and scaled sustainably.

column1: hrp,005056a3-d347-1fe1-a4c5-d4b465b362ad,16917303,Senior / Health Policy Analyst (Finance Partnerships & Governance) - Partnership,Ministry of Health,0000001200,"The Ministry of Health’s (MOH) vision is to champion a healthy nation with our people – to live well, live long and with peace of mind. MOH constantly grapples with new challenges brought on by an increasingly globalised world, a rapidly ageing population and rising expectations. MOH’s responses to these challenges include preventing and managing the outbreak of diseases such as SARS and Influenza A (H1N1), designing a healthcare system that delivers care in an integrated and effective manner, growing the capacity and capabilities within the sector, and managing healthcare inflation.

You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. Manage emergency operations and other duties as assigned to meet organisational objectives, including specifications review/input for new build/improvement projects concerning facility management and operations.

","

[What the role is]
Reporting to MPA's Hydrographic Division, candidate will be part of our team of maritime professionals whose responsibilities are to ensure safe navigation in Singapore waters by providing hydrographic, cartographic and aids to navigation products and services. ","

Your duties will include:

  • Prepare survey reports
  • Explore, assess and adopt new technologies (e.g. uncrewed platforms, AI and digital automation) to support hydrographic surveys
  • Procurement of hydrographic survey equipment and services.

","

Candidate should possess relevant certification in disciplines such as Engineering, Surveying, Nautical Studies, Information Technology, Geomatics or Geospatial Information Sciences.

Candidates with no prior experience are welcomed to apply. Candidates with relevant experience in these areas may be offered positions at a higher level.

|People, Our Pride | Service, Our Pledge | Integrity, Our Core | Excellence, Our Quest |",1636070400000,253402214400000,,,Permanent/Contract,0003,Entry level,0,0,Policy & Planning,0028,Policy & Planning,0021,Public Service Leadership,03,false,,"The Singapore Public Service offers an attractive career proposition for those who seek to make a difference in service of Singapore and Singaporeans.

We therefore welcome leaders with different backgrounds, who wish to contribute their skills and perspectives in the Public Service to make a meaningful impact to Singapore and Singaporeans.

If you take up a public service leadership career, we will invest in your development so that you can lead effectively in the Public Service, for today and tomorrow. A key feature of pursuing a public service leadership career is the opportunity for you to undergo structured job postings across different public agencies, to expose you to critical job experiences and key issues facing Government.

For individuals with more extensive working experience, please refer to the next section on the Mid-Career Leadership Track.
You can obtain updates on the status of your application through the same portal. For shortlisted candidates, PSD will contact you to provide details of the selection process.
• Mid-Career Leadership Track (MCLT) •

The Public Service values the experiences of mid-career entrants outside of the Public Service and is interested to groom talents with the heart to serve. The Public Service will be introducing the “Mid-Career Leaders Track” - a central gateway for mid-career entrants with the potential and aspiration to serve in Public Service leadership.
Key Features of MCLT:
• Central gateway for mid-career entrants to apply for Leadership Programmes in the Public Service

- Candidates may be considered for the PSLP Sectoral Phase (SP) or the Administrative Service (AS), where they would be supported in deepening their competencies either within a sector (PSLP SP) or across 2-3 sectors (AS).

- Candidates can apply without needing to choose to join the AS/PSLP or any specific government agencies. Successful candidates will be placed onto the appropriate leadership programme, where their past work experiences will be taken into account when curating relevant postings / developmental opportunities, based on the assessed calibre, readiness and seniority.

- The AS aims to develop multi-sectoral leaders with whole-of-government perspectives and capabilities, to formulate and implement policies that will improve the lives of Singaporeans. The career path of the AS can be found here.

- The PSLP aims to develop sectoral leaders for key leadership positions within the Public Service. There are 2 phases in this talent development programme. You will go through structured rotations during the General Phase to explore and gain experience in at least two different sectors of the Public Service, while at the Sectoral Phase, you will focus your development within a sector, building deeper competencies and networks. The career path of the PSLP can be found here.
• Structured job placement and onboarding support to support mid-career officers’ transition to the Public Service

- For their first one or two postings, officers on the MCLT will select from a list of curated jobs that provides developmental exposure while having adjacencies to their previous work experience. This allows officers to leverage their expertise and experiences in making substantive contributions, while supporting their learning and transition into the Public Service. Officers can look forward to a meaningful career journey across a variety of postings such as job roles in policy-operations as well as stakeholder mobilisation and engagement, which will tap on officers’ knowledge, skills and perspectives.

- A tailored onboarding experience with structured and personalised onboarding process to support officers’ transition on the MCLT. This is especially for working professions without any prior experience working in the Public Service.
You can apply for the MCLT by clicking on the ""Apply"" button.
For more information on the PSLC, please visit https://www.psd.gov.sg/leadership/public-service-leadership-careers for further clarification.",Others,Full-time

The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) was established on 2 February 1996, with the mission to develop Singapore as a premier global hub port and international maritime centre (IMC), and to advance and safeguard Singapore's strategic maritime interests. MPA is the driving force behind Singapore's port and maritime development, taking on the roles of Port Authority, Port Regulator, Port Planner, IMC Champion, and National Maritime Representative.

You will be part of MPA’s Strategy & Policy function which helps to drive MPA’s medium to long term direction to achieve Maritime Singapore’s vision as the world’s leading maritime hub. As a member of the Hub Strategy team, you will shape maritime strategies through the application of economics thinking, conducting of economic analysis, and forecasting of market trends. As part of this portfolio, you will also have the opportunity to be exposed to a diverse range of issues, as well as work on both qualitative and quantitative research projects to analyse strategic issues and facilitate management’s decision-making.

","

Responsibilities:

The role of Assistant Manager / Manager / Senior Manager for the Hub Strategy Department includes (but is not limited to):

  • Conduct research and surveillance of global/domestic economic trends (e.g. trade flows, value-add, productivity) and maritime developments (e.g. supply chains, freight markets).

  • Conduct quantitative and qualitative analysis to provide meaningful insights and assess the implications on Maritime Singapore.

  • Forecast trends and develop frameworks/models to stimulate different perspectives/scenarios.

  • Prepare reports and presentations to effectively communicate analytical findings to stakeholders.

","

  • Strong analytical (both quantitative and qualitative) skills, with passion to acquire knowledge in a diverse range of issues, and the ability to think critically and develop thoughtful opinions.

  • Good quantitative skills (e.g. econometrics, data science) for forecasting, modelling, impact assessments.

  • Good interpersonal and communication skills, as well as able to work effectively in teams.

  • Highly proficient with Microsoft Excel and other Office software such as Word and PowerPoint. Experience or familiarity in programming languages and software such as Python and Power BI is an advantage.

The Senior / Geospatial Manager is a key member of the Geospatial Services team, driving geospatial capability building across Singapore. ","

As a Senior Geospatial Product Manager, you will lead the delivery of geospatial solutions and oversee the ongoing management of the ArcGIS Enterprise ecosystem. You will balance technical platform oversight with the structured management of complex, multi-stakeholder projects, while maintaining a strategic view of how the platform should evolve to meet the needs of the public sector. We are looking for a highly organised, process-driven professional who can drive high-impact geospatial solutions to government agencies and identify future opportunities — including the integration of AI and machine learning — to unlock deeper analytical value.

Key Responsibilities

Project & Product Delivery: Own the full project lifecycle with rigour — from initial requirements gathering and scoping through to final deployment — ensuring all geospatial solutions are fit for purpose, delivered on time, and within scope.

Platform Oversight & Administration: Oversee the technical management of the solutions on ArcGIS Enterprise Portal, including platform administration, user access control, content management, and configuration, ensuring a seamless and secure experience for government users.

Technical Consultation & Solutioning: Engage with senior stakeholders across the Healthcare, Social, Education, and Government sectors to translate organisational needs into structured geospatial workplans and clearly defined technical requirements, including identifying opportunities where AI can augment geospatial analysis and decision-making.

Solution Configuration: Drive the development and configuration of geospatial applications, applying your technical depth to solve spatial problems for agencies across the public sector.

Capability & Training: Lead the design and delivery of geospatial programmes and technical workshops, effectively upskilling both technical and non-technical audiences in modern GIS workflows and emerging AI-augmented geospatial capabilities.

Strategic Communication: Champion geospatial technology as a persuasive advocate, translating technical complexity into clear, value-driven business cases for senior management and decision-makers.

","

The ideal candidate is a technically grounded professional with 8 to 10 years of relevant experience, with a proven track record of bridging technical development and executive-level project and product management. A forward-looking awareness of how AI and machine learning are reshaping the geospatial landscape is strongly desired.

Technical Requirements & Expertise

ArcGIS Platform Knowledge: Advanced, hands-on experience with ArcGIS Enterprise Portal administration and configuration is mandatory. You should be deeply familiar with the ESRI suite, including ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and associated extension tools, as well as the ArcGIS API for Python for workflow automation.

Development & Automation: Proficiency in Python and JavaScript is required to drive automation and support geospatial solution development. Familiarity with R is an advantage.

Geospatial Analytics: A solid technical understanding of geospatial concepts, data fusion techniques, and advanced spatial analytical methods.

AI & Machine Learning Awareness: A working understanding of how AI and machine learning techniques can be applied in a geospatial context is highly desirable. This includes familiarity with spatial predictive modelling, automated feature extraction from imagery, or the use of Python-based AI/ML libraries. Hands-on experience in this area is a strong advantage, though candidates with a clear aptitude and willingness to develop these skills will also be considered.

Open Source: Experience with QGIS is considered a bonus.

Project Management & Leadership

Process-Driven Management: Strong organisational skills with demonstrated experience managing full project lifecycles and vendor relationships. A formal project management certification (such as PMP, etc) is highly advantageous.

Business Analysis: Strong skills in requirements gathering, solution scoping, and stakeholder alignment, ensuring that technical solutions are grounded in practical business needs.

Communication: Ability to produce compelling, high-quality presentation decks and articulate complex geospatial and AI concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders at all levels.

Collaborative Leadership: Proven ability to build and manage diverse, cross-functional working relationships across multiple government agencies and teams, driving delivery in a collaborative environment.

hrp,005056a3-d347-1fe1-96a4-39ec918da2a7,17623006,SCDF Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) - 3 Year Contract,MHA - Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF),0000001086,"The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. hrp,005056a3-d347-1fe1-93c8-0643d66082a2,17565357,Manager/Senior Manager (Singapore Maritime Crisis Centre,Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore,0000009045,"""The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) was established on 2 February 1996, with the mission to develop Singapore as a premier global hub port and international maritime centre (IMC), and to advance and safeguard Singapore's strategic maritime interests.
MPA is the driving force behind Singapore's port and maritime development, taking on the roles of Port Authority, Port Regulator, Port Planner, IMC Champion, and National Maritime Representative.

The officer plays a key role towards the Whole-of-Government approach to detect and deter maritime security (MARSEC) threats in the Port of Singapore and Singapore Territorial Water (STW). Maritime Security is important to safeguard Singapore’s strategic maritime interest and maintains Singapore’s status as the premier hub port as well as the international maritime centre.

","

Working closely with stakeholders, the officer is required to provide insights on maritime security and regulatory matters to support sharper sense-making to plan for a successful maritime operation. The officer will also be the key liaison between MPA departments and the seconded agency to ensure cross-agency initiatives are well communicated and executed. The officer will be required to support the conduct of exercises and workshops as well as training sessions/ visits/ seminars to enhance the Maritime organisation’s awareness and knowledge of the shipping industry.

Other operational duties can also include :

• Representing MPA on maritime security issues with other government agencies at various committees, working groups, and taking turns to perform secretariat function for these working groups etc

• Part of the planning and execution team for the Whole-of-Government (WoG) maritime security operations for key coastal events, where the officer is required to be the MPA Liaison Officer and perform duties during these Maritime operations to ensure the security of major national events, which may fall on weekends and public holidays.

• Performing Duty Officer duties (12hrs duty both day and night shift at the Command Centre) on an average of 4 times per month to manage incidents and ensure smooth operations

","

• Strong analytical, writing, communication and interpersonal skills, as well as able to work efficiently in teams

• Highly driven, organized, and able to manage multiple priorities

• Good knowledge of the shipping/ marine industry, with prior experience in this industry would be an advantage

• Candidate with working experience in related security functions in the military or national security agencies as well as good understanding of the National Maritime Security System framework will have an advantage.

• Candidate's job title at Singapore Maritime Crisis Centre (SMCC) will be in accordance with SMCC's job title framework.

  • Developing a thorough understanding of engineering workflows and processes across the organisation, building a clear picture of functional needs and priority pain points.
  • Defining and maintaining a structured framework of GIS use cases organised by common workflows, user groups, and data needs — mapping existing solutions against this framework to identify gaps, duplication, and opportunities for standardisation.
  • Designing and maintaining reusable GIS templates and solution frameworks, including for areas not yet served by existing tools, and assessing enterprise systems and platforms to ensure GIS solutions are fit for purpose.
  • Creating clear, task-based user guides and quick-start materials to help non-expert users get up and running with reusable templates.
  • Planning and leading outreach initiatives across Groups to showcase GIS capabilities, gather feedback, and drive uptake — including facilitating workshops and clinics to support users, address technical queries, and foster knowledge sharing.
  • Continuously scanning for opportunities to broaden the application of GIS across the organisation, translating these into proposed pilots, standards, or roadmap items.

","

  • Strong ability to elicit requirements from users, understand end-to-end workflows, and translate them into practical, scalable solutions — from prototype through to full rollout.
  • Hands-on experience creating reusable GIS assets such as templates, data models, map and app patterns, symbology standards, and reference architectures.
  • Working knowledge of enterprise applications and data platforms — such as EAM/CMMS, document management systems, BIM/CAD tools, and data lakes — and how GIS integrates with them.

  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills, with the ability to facilitate alignment and influence outcomes across teams without relying on formal authority.
  • A proactive and strategic mindset — with the ability to spot opportunities, prioritise value, and drive continuous improvement through well-designed standards and reusable solutions.

Your work will have far-reaching impact on the health and lives of Singaporeans.",1780876800000,1787184000000,Closing in 4 day(s),1  week(s) ago,Permanent/Contract,0003,03-05 year(s),3,5,Policy & Planning,0025,Policy & Planning,0021,Others,00,false,,"The Division:

Singapore keeps healthcare affordable through government subsidies and the 3Ms: MediShield Life, MediSave and MediFund. For these schemes to work, every part of the supporting systems must function accurately and without interruption. The Finance Systems Policy (FSP) division at MOH owns the systems that make this possible. These include the National Platform for Healthcare Claims, means-testing systems administering healthcare subsidise such as the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS), and the accreditation framework that governs which institutions and practitioners may participate in financing schemes. Together, these systems process tens of thousands of claims daily and form the operational backbone of Singapore's healthcare financing architecture.
The Role:

Your starting assignment is the Financing Schemes Accreditation E-service (FSAE) system. Before a patient can use MediSave or MediShield Life at a medical institution, that institution and its practitioners must be accredited by MOH. FSAE manages that process: it handles accreditation applications, verifications, and decisions for medical institutions and practitioners across Singapore. The system operates across multiple agencies, including the Central Provident Fund Board (CPFB), the Singapore Medical Council (SMC), the Singapore Dental Council (SDC), and the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) and so on.

A practitioner who cannot submit claims means a patient who cannot access financing for their treatments. Keeping accreditation accurate, expedient, and aligned with policy is what this role exists to do.
Over time, as you develop your understanding of FSP's portfolio, there is scope to take on other systems within the division. The capabilities you build on one system transfer directly to others.
You will be working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time","Product Ownership

You will be responsible for FSAE and its related accreditation systems end-to-end. This means understanding what each system does, why it was designed the way it was, where it falls short, and how it can be improved. You will work with MOH policy teams, IT vendors, and technical teams to translate requirements into system design, develop and prioritise the feature roadmap, conduct usability and end-to-end testing, and ensure that changes work as intended before they reach end-users.
Policy-to-System Translation

Healthcare financing schemes evolve continuously. New services become claimable. Accreditation criteria are updated. Licensing requirements change under the Healthcare Services Act. Each change requires someone who understands both the policy intent and the system's behaviour well enough to ensure nothing is lost in translation. This thread is a distinct part of the role, not a subset of product ownership.
Operational Continuity

Accreditation is not a set-and-forget process. Institutions encounter issues. Data needs to be reviewed and sometimes corrected. Systemic problems need to be identified, traced, and resolved before they compound. You will maintain oversight of day-to-day system health, manage data access and sharing in accordance with whole-of-government data governance guidelines, and handle requests from external stakeholders appropriately.
This is not a delivery coordination role. It requires genuine ownership of both the policy intent behind a system and the technical design that carries it out.
The Team:
You will report to an Assistant Director in FSP and work within a division of about 14 officers.

FSP runs a structured capability development programme for its officers, built around four areas: product thinking, policy domain knowledge, communications, and technical skills. In practical terms, this means that 18 months in, you should be able to read a policy paper and interrogate whether FSAE's design actually implements it, hold your own in a technical review with a vendor, and produce a brief that helps Senior Management make a good decision.","We are looking for someone with 3 to 5 years of working experience in policy, operations, technology, or a field that required you to translate between these domains.

column2: Thinking Clearly and Making Sound Judgements.  In FSP, this means tracing why a system behaves the way it does, identifying where it diverges from policy intent, and forming a clear recommendation with the evidence available, not the evidence you wish you had.
