HCC is located in a purpose-built facility that serves as the centralised storage and conservation labs for the National Collection of Singapore. The National Collection encompasses a wide range of art and heritage objects, including but not limited to decorative objects, social history objects, contemporary art installations, industrial and technical heritage objects, musical instruments, and re-functionalised objects.
Currently, the Conservation Services department at HCC comprises 6 conservation specialisations organised in sections: Inorganic Objects; Organic Objects; Paintings; Paper, Photographs & Digital Media; Textiles; and Conservation Science. HCC is now recruiting a Senior Conservator/ Head of Section (Inorganic Objects) to lead the Inorganic Objects conservation section.

","

  • Manage section staffing, including the hiring and selection of conservators and interns.

  • Contribute to the management of the Conservation Services department and facilitate work across departments and divisions in NHB, while closely working with the other Heads of Sections and leaders of relevant working groups.   • Represent HCC in collaborations with other institutions as and when required, to advance its reputation as a leader on conservation matters, locally, regionally and internationally.

  • Oversee and provide advice on conservation work undertaken by conservators in the Inorganic Objects section, including collections care, conservation treatments, scientific analyses, and project management.

  • Ensure that conservation guidelines and standards of practice for a holistic approach to collections care and access are based on current ethics and principles, and that they are timely and adequately implemented by the section within allocated resources.

  • Set research directions for the section that are aligned with the overall research priorities of the Conservation Services department, and supervise and drive the resulting research activities in the section.

  • Oversee and drive outreach activities of the section relating to collections care and conservation, which may include areas of professional collaboration, education, and capability development, involving both professional and non-professional target audiences that are internal or external to HCC and NHB.

Operational functions

hrp,005056a3-53e2-1fd1-96e0-53b6409433f8,17631828,SCDF Fire and Rescue Officer (Direct-Entry Lieutenant),MHA - Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF),0000001086,"The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. [What the role is]

You are the technical engine of our data exploration efforts. In the fast-paced world of tourism, new data opportunities emerge constantly, but their true value is often locked away. Your mission is to be the key that unlocks it.

This role is the technical counterpart to our Data Partnership Managers, forming a dynamic duo to accelerate our data pilots. While the Partnership Manager defines the business problem/opportunity and secures the data, you will deep-dive into the data - to wrangle the data, test hypotheses, and build compelling proof-of-concept dashboards and analyses. You are the ""technical expert"" in our ""tech sales"" model.

Success in this position means rapidly transforming raw, messy data from new data pilots and data partnerships into tangible, high-impact prototypes that showcase the possibilities and maximum potential we can achieve with our data. You will deliver the evidence and initial insights that determine which data pilots graduate to become scaled, industry-wide data products.

This contract role sits within the Data Exploration and Partnerships (DXP) department. We are looking for a data practitioner who is passionate in data exploration, experimentation, and moving quickly to create tangible impact.

","

[What you will be working on]

Technical Design & Feasibility Assessment:

  • Partner with Data Partnership Managers in later-stage discussions with potential data partners to finalise the scope and specifications of data exchange.

  • Act as the technical expert, assessing the quality, structure, and feasibility of using STB’s and our partner's data.

  • Help translate business problems into specific, testable analytical questions.

Hands-on Data Analysis & Prototyping:

  • Take the lead on the entire technical pilot process: data ingestion, cleaning, and transformation of new and diverse datasets.

  • Perform advanced exploratory data analysis (EDA) using Python to uncover hidden patterns, correlations, and insights that go beyond basic reporting.

  • Apply statistical methods to test hypotheses with rigour and build simple predictive models where applicable.

  • Lead technical discovery and experimentation, defining your own hypotheses and analytical approaches to uncover the most valuable insights.

  • Design and build compelling, interactive proof-of-concept dashboards (using tools like AWS QuickSight) that answer business questions clearly to non-technical stakeholders.

Insight Generation & Storytelling:

  • Synthesize complex analytical findings into clear, concise insights and recommendations.

  • Collaborate with the Data Partnership Manager to present pilot findings back to internal and external stakeholders, demonstrating the value of the data collaboration.

  • Where possible and relevant, stretch the data pilots to include predictive and prescriptive insight.

Knowledge Transfer & Scaling Preparation:

  • Meticulously document the data sources, cleaning logic, analytical methodologies, and code for successful pilots.

  • Create a "recipe book" for each successful pilot that enables a smooth handover to the Data & AI Product Manager for evaluation and potential productisation onto our core Data and Analytics platform, STAN.

","

[What we are looking for]

Technical and Analytics skills:

  • Trained in a quantitative field such as Data Analytics, Computer Science, Statistics, Engineering, or Economics.

  • At least 3 years of demonstrable, hands-on experience in exploratory data analysis, data ingestion, transformation (cleaning, aggregation), and data modeling using large, real-world datasets.

  • Strong proficiency in statistical programming (e.g., Python) and database scripting (SQL) is essential.

  • Proven ability to develop compelling data visualizations and dashboards. Experience with tools like AWS QuickSight is highly advantageous.

  • Solid applied statistical knowledge (e.g., regression, classification, significance testing).

  • A portfolio of projects (e.g., via GitHub, a personal website, or a slide deck) showcasing your hands-on data analysis and coding work is required.

Work Approach:

  • Collaborative Partner: A strong team player who sees yourself as the technical counterpart to our business-facing managers. You are comfortable owning your technical workstream end-to-end while working closely with others to achieve a shared goal.

  • Comfortable with Ambiguity: A self-starter who thrives in an environment where priorities evolve and the path isn't always clear. You can take a vague business problem and messy data, and proactively find a path forward without waiting for instructions.

  • Accountable & Driven: Balance creativity and exploration with discipline and follow-through. You take ownership of your projects, manage your timelines effectively, and are responsible for communicating progress and challenges clearly.

  • The Pragmatic Storyteller: Strong analytical skills with a good eye for detail, but you also know how to translate complex technical findings into clear, concise language that a business audience can understand and act upon.

  • A Continuous Learner: Humble and curious, open to feedback, new techniques, and better ways of working in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.

This is not simply an audit leadership role — you will be a change agent, driving the evolution of IA practices across the public sector through digital innovation, agile methodologies, and a broadened risk lens that encompasses technology, cybersecurity, and sustainability. You will shape the future of the public sector IA community by building capabilities, professionalising practices, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement and intellectual curiosity.","Strategic Audit Leadership

You will direct the planning, management, and execution of risk-based audit engagements across agencies under AGD's portfolio of clients, ensuring timely delivery and consistently high audit quality. Moving beyond traditional compliance-focused auditing, you will develop and maintain a forward-looking audit universe that reflects emerging risks and align audit priorities with the broader governance and risk landscape of the public sector. You will also champion agile auditing methodologies, designing shorter and more iterative audit cycles that deliver faster, more actionable insights to stakeholders.
Digital Transformation

You will lead the integration of data analytics, robotic process automation (RPA), and AI-assisted audit tools into the audit methodology to enable continuous monitoring and deeper audit insights. You will oversee the adoption of audit management platforms to improve workflow efficiency and documentation standards. Staying ahead of developments in generative AI, machine learning, and other emerging technologies, you will assess their applicability to the IA function and build the team's capacity to leverage these tools effectively. Experience with data analytics tools such as Power BI, or Python in an audit context will be particularly valued.
Emerging Risk and Advisory

As a strategic advisor, you will engage credibly with C-suite and senior public sector leadership, translating complex audit findings into clear, business-relevant insights that drive meaningful governance improvements. You will provide assurance and advisory perspectives on a broadened risk landscape, including IT general controls, cybersecurity risk, digital business processes, third-party and supply chain risk, and increasingly, sustainability and ESG governance frameworks. You will work closely with agency leadership to anticipate risks before they materialise, positioning IA as a forward-looking function rather than a retrospective one.
Community Building and Capability Development

You will work with IA heads across the public sector to build a vibrant community of practice, driving the development of shared frameworks, toolkits, and upskilling programmes that raise the overall standard of public sector IA. You will implement capability development roadmaps that equip IA practitioners with both technical audit competencies and digital skills — including data literacy, AI fluency, and agile ways of working. You will represent AGD in cross-agency forums and professional bodies to advance the ambition of public sector IA.
People Leadership and Culture

You will manage, mentor, and develop a team of IA professionals, building a pipeline of future audit leaders who are technically strong, digitally capable, and strategically minded. You will foster a team culture that values psychological safety, diversity of thought, intellectual curiosity, and a genuine commitment to public service excellence. Attracting and retaining talent in a competitive market will be an important part of your mandate.","•
column2: A strong background in accountancy or a related discipline is essential, along with at least 10 years of progressive audit experience with a meaningful portion in a leadership capacity.

At the Energy Market Authority (EMA), we do more than keep the lights on. As Singapore's energy market regulator and industry developer, we work to ensure a reliable, secure and sustainable energy supply for homes, businesses and the economy.

As Singapore's energy landscape evolves, delivering excellent public service is increasingly important in building trust and confidence with our stakeholders. We are committed to building a customer-centric organisation through better service design, stronger service capabilities and continuous improvement.

What the Role is

As part of the Digital Communications and Customer Experience Department, you will play a key role in advancing EMA's Service Excellence agenda by driving organisation-wide initiatives that strengthen customer-centricity and improve service delivery.

You will partner stakeholders across the agency to identify opportunities for service redesign, capability building and continuous improvement. The role also oversees customer operations and case management, ensuring operational insights and digital solutions are leveraged to enhance service quality and customer experience.

","

What You Will be Working On

Service Excellence & Customer Experience

  • Drive organisation-wide Service Excellence initiatives to strengthen customer-centricity and improve service delivery across EMA.
  • Design and implement capability-building programmes, frameworks, and resources that embed customer-centric practices across the organisation.
  • Review customer journeys, service touchpoints, and internal processes to identify opportunities for service redesign and continuous improvement.
  • Leverage customer insights, operational data and feedback to drive service improvement initiatives, including customer journey mapping, and service audits.
  • Support organisation-wide service excellence programmes and related governance committees.

Customer Operations, Case Management & Service Governance

  • Oversee the outsourced contact centre to ensure service standards and customer experience outcomes are consistently achieved.
  • Monitor customer enquiries, appeals and case trends to identify systemic issues and opportunities for service improvement.
  • Drive the enhancement of customer case management capabilities, including reviewing business requirements, leading the procurement and implementation of a case management system, and improving case management processes.
  • Analyse service performance, customer feedback and operational trends to provide insights that support management decision-making and continuous improvement.

","

What We Are Looking For

We are looking for someone who is passionate about improving customer experiences and driving organisation-wide service excellence.

The ideal candidate should have:

  • At least 3 years' relevant experience in Service Excellence, Service Transformation, Continuous Improvement, Service Design, Customer Experience or related fields.
  • Demonstrated experience driving organisation-wide service improvement or customer-centric initiatives beyond day-to-day customer service operations. Experience in areas such as service redesign, customer journey mapping, design thinking, or capability-building initiatives will be an advantage.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to translate customer feedback, operational data and service trends into actionable recommendations.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement, communication and project management skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders across different functions.
  • A proactive and collaborative mindset, with a passion for service excellence, continuous improvement and innovation.
  • Comfortable leveraging digital technologies and AI-enabled solutions to enhance service delivery and operational efficiency.
  • Prior public sector experience will be an advantage.
",Others,Full-time

As an investigator in the Enforcement Department, your primary responsibility is to investigate into offences and/or regulatory breaches under all MAS-administered Acts. You will be gazetted as a Commercial Affairs Officer with criminal investigative powers under the MAS-CAD Joint Investigation Arrangement, where you will exercise comprehensive criminal investigative powers, including searching premises, seizures of evidence and effecting arrests during raid operations.

Your responsibilities encompass thorough evidence gathering, conducting interviews, handling of bail procedures and preparing detailed case files as well as providing litigation support to the Attorney-General's Chambers in both criminal prosecutions and civil penalty court actions. Additionally, you will be involved in enforcing regulatory actions, such as issuing prohibition orders to not allow offenders from working in Singapore's financial industry and handling regulatory appeals.

Specifically to the current role, you will specialise primarily in market abuse cases such as insider trading, market manipulation, and breaches of continuous disclosure requirements under Part XII of the Securities and Futures Act. As financial crimes are often complex and multi-faceted, you would be working closely with fellow investigation officers, and other specialists within the Enforcement Department such as market surveillance analysts, computer forensic specialists, legal officers, as well as officers from the Commercial Affairs Department, market experts/professionals and Deputy Public Prosecutors from the Attorney-General's Chambers.

","

column1: hrp,005056a3-53e2-1fd1-a5d1-6d1e7e987402,17214768,[Agency Contract] Principal Exec/Snr Exec (Governance & Admin),Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore,0000009045,"""The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) was established on 2 February 1996, with the mission to develop Singapore as a premier global hub port and international maritime centre (IMC), and to advance and safeguard Singapore's strategic maritime interests.
MPA is the driving force behind Singapore's port and maritime development, taking on the roles of Port Authority, Port Regulator, Port Planner, IMC Champion, and National Maritime Representative.

MPA partners the industry and other agencies to enhance safety, security and environmental protection in our port waters, facilitate port operations and growth, expand the cluster of maritime ancillary services, and promote maritime R&D and manpower development.""",1772496000000,1788048000000,Closing on 30 Aug 2026,5 day(s) ago,Fixed Terms,0006,01-01 year(s),1,1,Corporate Administration,0002,Corporate Administration,0005,Administration Support,00,false,,"

What the role is:
You will be part of a dynamic team that drives transformation of Singapore's maritime industry and grows Singapore as a Global Leading Maritime Technology Hub. The Governance & Administration (GA) team develops and maintains effective governance and efficient processes for the industry funds, grant schemes, programmes, and MOUs under the Innovation, Technology and Talent Development division.

This is a 1 year contract position under recruitment agency.

","

What you will be working on:

As part of the GA team, your key duties and responsibilities include:

(a) Grant Processing and Administration

- Process grant claims and disbursements, including reviewing documentations, clarifying requirements with grant applicants and project managers, and issuing offer letters.

(b) Data Management and Reporting

- Assist the GA team in data collection and reporting to senior management and stakeholders.

(c) Administrative and Operational Support

- Support the division's finance/budgeting and procurement functions, while providing administrative and logistics support to the division. This includes calendar management, organising meetings/events, supporting the division's knowledge management, and system access management.

(d) You will also play a supporting role in the following areas:

i. Reviewing and implementing policies, guidelines, SOPs, and templates that enhance the division's objectives and processes.

ii. Reporting and presenting KPIs of the division's industry funds to the MPA Board, management meetings and stakeholders.

iii. Developing and managing the division's grant management system and anomaly/fraud detection system.

iv. Recommending and sourcing external funds that MPA could leverage for industry development.

v. Conducting industry consultations, surveys and interviews relating to the industry funds.

","

What we are looking for:

  • Minimum 2-3 years of relevant experience in grants administration, project management, or government operations
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint)
  • Experience with data analysis and report preparation
  • Self-motivated with ability to work independently and as part of a team
  • Strong organisational skills and ability to prioritise competing demands
  • Customer service orientation when dealing with grant applicants and stakeholders
  • Continuous learning mindset to stay updated with industry trends and regulatory changes

",Others,Full-time

[What the role is]

STB takes a data-driven approach in tourism planning and marketing, and at the heart of it is Stan (Singapore Tourism Analytics Network, Stan), a tourism data analytics platform that allows both internal STB users and external tourism industry stakeholders to access tourism data and derive actionable insights about Singapore's tourism landscape and visitors.

As Data and AI Product Manager, you will play a pivotal role in building the data product roadmap for STB and its industry stakeholders to drive tourism growth. You'll be at the forefront of leveraging data and AI to transform Singapore's tourism industry, not just defining what needs to be built, but getting hands-on to prove it works before it scales. Success in this position means delivering data and AI-enabled products that measurably enhance tourism decision-making capabilities, with demonstrated user adoption, stakeholder satisfaction, and measurable business impact on Singapore's tourism sector.

This role sits within the newly established Data Exploration and Partnerships department, reporting directly to the Head of Department, and works closely with line units across Singapore Tourism Board, government agencies, and industry partners to drive data-driven decision-making and insights generation in tourism.

","

[What you will be working on]

As a Data and AI Product Manager, your key responsibilities include:

1. Data Products Roadmap Development, Planning and Execution:

a) Develop and execute the data product roadmap, defining data products required by STB and industry stakeholders, and aligned with STB's organisational goals.

b) Create and maintain comprehensive data products requirement specifications, acceptance criteria and test cases.

c) Develop mock and/or POC dashboards and datasets, to support requirements specifications and acceptance criteria.

d) Work with Stan product team to plan and implement the data products onto Stan.

e) Support testing and production verification as part of productisation process.

f) Lead product launches and go-to-market plans for major releases of data products.

g) Drive innovation in data products, constantly seeking ways to enhance value for stakeholders.

h) Proactively identify opportunities for new data products or features based on industry trends and stakeholder needs.

2. AI Roadmap, Use Cases and Proof-of-Concept Development

a) Ideate and develop the AI roadmap for STB's data platforms, identifying high-value AI use cases that enhance data accessibility and user productivity for internal and industry stakeholders.

b) Prioritise AI roadmap items using sound evaluation frameworks that weigh feasibility, impact, and implementation readiness.

c) Lead hands-on development of AI proof-of-concepts, starting with natural language query (NLQ) for conversational access to STB's datasets and analytics.

d) Design evaluation frameworks, guardrails, and test cases for AI features, ensuring reliability, accuracy, and appropriateness before productisation.

e) Identify and shape AI use cases in close collaboration with line units, translating domain needs into technically grounded AI applications.

f) Work closely with the product implementation team to ensure AI PoCs are documented and specified to a standard that enables direct handover for productisation.

g) Stay current on applied AI developments relevant to data platforms, analytics, and public sector use cases.

3. Requirements Gathering and Product Design:

a) Conduct deep dives into business scenarios, use cases, user journey mapping as part of data and AI product solution design.

b) Translate complex stakeholder needs into clear, actionable product requirements and specifications.

c) Collaborate with Data Partnerships and Stan product team to ensure product feasibility and technical alignment.

d) As part of data and AI product design and specifications, review the end-to-end processes involved in implementing and maintaining the data products, ensure processes are streamlined and efficient.

e) Leverage digital and automation tools where possible as part of the end-to-end process design i.e. WOG tools like FormSG and Plumber to automate data collection and simple data validation checks.

4. Data Governance and Quality Management for Industry-facing data domains:

a) Ensure adherence to data governance policies for data integrity, security, and compliance.

b) Support data quality management processes, ensuring the accuracy and reliability of data products as part of productisation process.

c) Apply appropriate guardrails and evaluation criteria to AI features to ensure outputs meet governance and quality standards.

5. Stakeholder Management and Communication:

a) Build and maintain strong relationships with stakeholders across STB line units, government agencies, and industry partners, with varying levels of data and tech maturity.

b)Translate complex data and AI concepts into clear, structured communications for non-technical stakeholders, facilitating understanding and buy-in.

c) Drive alignment and clarity across stakeholders, ensuring well-defined problem statements, expectations, and outcomes.

d) Collaborate cross-functionally to ensure alignment between product development, business needs, and technical capabilities.

e) Facilitate structured discussions and decision-making, especially in ambiguous or exploratory problem spaces.

6. Analytics, Experimentation and Continuous Improvement:

a) Support data pilots in identifying and solving complex data-related problems, applying critical thinking and analytical skills.

b) Support data pilots in advanced analytics, data integration and data wrangling needs.

c) Define and track key performance indicators (KPIs) for data products implemented.

d) Analyze usage pattern, stakeholder feedback and performance metrics to inform continuous improvement.

","

The ideal candidate is formally trained in Business, Data Science, Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, with at least 3–5 years of experience in data product management, data engineering, or related roles with a proven track record of delivering data-driven solutions.

Essential Skills and Knowledge

-Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to break down ambiguous problems into clear, actionable components, and navigate uncertainty with confidence.

-Experience evaluating pilot projects and experimental initiatives for scalability and productisation potential.

-Familiarity with data governance frameworks, data quality management, and regulatory compliance requirements.

Technical Skills

-Strong data analytics capabilities, including data exploration, transformation, and dashboard development, with proficiency in tools such as AWS QuickSight.

-Proficient in SQL and at least one programming language (Python or R).

-Hands-on experience developing or prototyping AI use cases, including prompt design, evaluation of AI outputs, and simple workflows.

-Ability to design evaluation frameworks for AI outputs, including defining metrics, test cases, and guardrails.

-Familiar with data structures and modelling required to support AI-driven use cases.

Product Management

-Proven product management skills spanning roadmap development, requirements gathering, UX design, and go-to-market execution.

-Demonstrated ability to drive products from concept to pilot to production, translating learnings into structured outcomes.

-Comfortable balancing strategic thinking with hands-on execution in early-stage product environments.

Professional Attributes

-Structured and rigorous, bringing clear frameworks and logic to complex or ambiguous problems.

-Proactive in identifying gaps and opportunities, with strong stakeholder communication and alignment skills.

-Able to work independently in evolving environments while owning workstreams end to end.

-Collaborative, hands-on, and disciplined — balancing exploration with follow-through and a strong focus on end-user value.

Additional Qualifications

Experience in tourism, hospitality, or the public sector is advantageous. Familiarity with AWS QuickSight or similar cloud analytics platforms, data integration processes, API management, and AI application development (including prompt engineering or LLM evaluation) would be a plus. Relevant certifications in product management, data engineering, or AI/ML are welcome.

GovTech supports various Government Agencies in carrying out ICT delivery services and appoints Agency Chief Information Security Officers (ACISO) to oversee information security management within these agencies. The ACISO is a leadership role that requires technical proficiency demonstrated in multiple cybersecurity domains. The role demands knowledge and/or practical experience in most of the domains below:
<ul>
• Cybersecurity Governance frameworks,
<ul>
• Security Operations including incident response,
<ul>
• Architecture design and threat risk assessment,
<ul>
• Security Testing.

The ACISO must possess technical understanding of both on-premises infrastructure security and cloud security architectures across major platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, and GCP), including their native security features, identity management systems, and security control implementations.
[What you will be working on]

Emplaced in public agencies and reporting to the agency’s Chief Information Officer (CIO) and Ministry Family CISO, you will collaborate with various stakeholders (GovTech HQ teams, Agency management, Agency project teams, and outsourced vendors) and will be responsible to:
<ul>
• Lead the agency-level cybersecurity function in supporting agency digital transformation initiatives whilst ensuring digital resilience of agency systems.
<ul>
• Formulate and implement agency cybersecurity strategies, policies and work plans, ensuring continuous alignment with Ministry Family's business strategic goals
<ul>
• Review and enhance risk management through threat-based risk assessments, risk mitigations, risk monitoring and reporting.
<ul>
• Provide consultation and endorse risk management and mitigation plans from agency’s project teams.
<ul>
• Govern and enhance the agency's security posture by maintaining visibility and oversight of ICT assets, security architectures, and cybersecurity operations code of practices.
<ul>

• Develop and maintain incident response plan and playbooks. This involves planning, designing and conduct of security incident response workshops and exercises (table-top exercises, simulation and drills) as well as lead the investigation and management of ICT security incidents.
<ul>
• Provide advisory and recommendations on appropriate cybersecurity technologies to be deployed that meets agency’s business requirements and aligned with WOG-wide advisories and practices.
<ul>
• Ensure secure by design ICT product development, and that security controls implementations comply with the defined security policies, standards and guidelines.
<ul>
• Develop and maintain effective cybersecurity awareness and training programmes
[What we are looking for]
<ul>
• Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering or related Technology field
<ul>
• At least 8-10 years of management experience related to information security and solid grasp of ICT operations, security policies, business processes and the relationship between them.
<ul>
• Ability to work with multi-functional, multi-disciplined teams to formulate, institute real time awareness of security posture and baseline among end users.
<ul>
• Good interpersonal and partner/executive leadership skills.
<ul>
• Demonstrate knowledge and experience in security by design implementations, review of system architecture, devsecops practices, Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools and securing CI/CD pipelines
<ul>

• Demonstrate understanding of cloud service models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS), coupled with a strong understanding of core cloud services and modern cloud-native architectures (serverless, containers, microservices)
<ul>

• Identify on-premises and cloud-specific cybersecurity risks and threats, demonstrating skills to thoroughly assess their impact and likelihood. This assessment encompasses, but is not limited to, secure configurations, insider threats, vendor risks, data leakage, malwares including ransomware, account hijacking, and compliance risks.
<ul>
• Evaluate the effectiveness of existing controls and recommending appropriate mitigation strategies for on-premises and cloud-related cybersecurity and data security issues.
<ul>
• Display understanding of emerging threats and technologies, and the ability to translate risk into business impact
<ul>
• Strong understanding of compliance requirements and the ability to identify potential violations in on-premises or cloud environments.
<ul>
• Able to communicate cyber security topics effectively to senior stakeholders.
<ul>
• Minimally possess CISSP certification, preferably with other related certifications, e.g. CISM, CCSP, GCIH that demonstrates continuous learning and knowledge of industry best practices.
<ul>
• We believe in being Agile, Bold and Collaborative, and are looking for people who identify with these values.
<ul>
• Singaporeans only.

As the Design Lead, you will be the most senior designer across both programmes, responsible for driving distinct design visions within each while ensuring coherence and quality within them. The Design Lead will report to the Programme Director of both programmes.

<li>

<li>
Shape programme and product roadmaps, partnering with product and engineering leads to embed design principles into strategic decisions.
<li>
Mentor and empower designers to raise design standards, improve ways of working and encourage cross-team collaboration.
[Who we are looking for]
<ul data-pm-slice=""3 3 []"">
<li>
Seasoned design leader with experience leading the design of multiple complementary products or product suites.
<li>
Strategic thinker who can balance near-term delivery priorities with long-term product and experience vision.
<li>
Strong collaborator and influencer, adept at demonstrating the value of design to stakeholders through evidence and insight.
<li>
Thought leader in design craft and strategy, who can establish and evolve design principles, standards and visions as products mature.
Bonus points
Experience designing low-code or no-code SaaS platform solutions, or multi-product ecosystems that empower users to self-serve through configuration.

About Government Technology Agency
The Government Technology Agency (GovTech) is the lead agency driving Singapore’s Smart Nation initiatives and public sector digital transformation. Play a part in Singapore’s vision to build a Smart Nation and embark on your meaningful journey to build tech for public good. Join us to advance our mission and shape your future with us today! Learn more about GovTech at tech.gov.sg.
How We Think About Product Operations
Before describing the role, it is worth being clear about our beliefs — because they shape what we hire for, how we measure success, and what kind of leader we are looking for.

Product Operations exists to make it easier for product teams to deliver citizen-centric outcomes at scale, with precision and reliability. Where Product Managers focus on ""what"" and ""why"", Product Operations focuses on ""how well"" and ""how efficiently"" we deliver.
Role Overview

As an Assistant Director / Deputy Director of Product Operations in DXD (Digital Excellence & Products Division), you are accountable for designing, implementing, and driving adoption of product operations capabilities within a core digital vertical portfolio.

You are a senior leader who defines the vision and strategy for product operations across a cluster of agencies. You focus on operational excellence at scale — building frameworks that align with organisational strategy and enable efficient, consistent, and impactful product delivery. You partner with executive stakeholders, drive cross-functional alignment, mentor senior talent, and champion a culture of continuous improvement.

In the GovTech context, this means shifting the organisation from ad-hoc coordination structures to sustained operating cadences — portfolio reviews, cross-agency alignment forums, and scaled feedback systems that continuously inform product strategy across policy cycles and legacy environments.
Target Portfolio Scope
You will be accountable for end-to-end product operations across a core digital vertical portfolio or cluster of agencies, which may include:
<ul>
• Parents-facing applications and services
• Teacher professional learning and development platforms
• Student Learning Space (SLS) and related ecosystem products
• National placement and registration services (e.g. OnePlacement)
• Platform & Infrastructure (e.g. Data, AI and Identity Management)
• HQ functions (e.g. HR and Corporate Finance)
Within this scope, you will partner closely with business owners (e.g. schools, HQ divisions, Academy of Singapore Teachers) and align with central DXD standards and practices.
Key Responsibilities
Organised across the 5 core pillars of Product Ops at GovTech:
Strategic Partnership
<ul>
• Define and drive the Product Ops vision and strategy across a cluster of agencies, partner with executive stakeholders to align operational priorities with agency and Smart Nation objectives
• Position Product Ops as a force multiplier for PMs — co-owning outcome metrics like PM Strategic Time Index, launch success rates, and Playbook Standardisation Rate
• Drive development and implementation of operational strategies aligned with the mission of a cluster of agencies, own funding and procurement strategies at the cluster level
• Drive cross-agency strategies to proactively shape the impact of policy changes on product operations, oversee policy review processes and integrate them with operational frameworks
Data-Driven Insights
<ul>
• Drive a data-driven culture across agencies — championing the use of objective indicators in all governance, tooling, and process decisions
• Author cross-agency user research initiatives that inform and shape operational strategy at scale
• Build automated reporting and dashboarding systems that provide real-time visibility to product leadership, implement data governance and quality assurance processes that ensure trusted insights
• Hold the cluster accountable to the Product Ops scorecard: PM Strategic Time Index, Insights Activation Rate, Collaboration Health Score, Feedback-to-Feature Conversion Rate
Operational Excellence
<ul>
• Drive operational excellence across a cluster of agencies, lead development of cross-agency operating frameworks that enable consistent, high-quality product delivery
• Champion innovative practices that raise the standard of product performance across the cluster, conduct regular maturity assessments and drive continuous capability uplift
• Oversee robust risk management and incident management frameworks across agencies, ensuring compliance and operational resilience at scale
• Develop lightweight, scalable governance frameworks that provide clear product delivery oversight without creating bottlenecks, design quality assurance standards that reduce launch risk
Voice of Customer
<ul>
• Drive user support and engagement optimisation across multiple agencies, improving overall user satisfaction and product adoption
• Spearhead the design of scaled feedback infrastructure — ensuring user signals from citizens, educators, and students are systematically captured, triaged, and routed to inform product roadmaps
• Maintain closed-loop feedback processes that visibly connect user input to product decisions across the cluster
Cross-Functional Orchestration
<ul>
• Build and lead high-performing product operations teams across agencies, significantly elevate the function's capabilities at scale
• Drive cross-functional collaboration and alignment between practice leads on cluster-level operational strategies — ensuring everyone sees the same information and understands their decision rights
• Serve as a formal mentor to senior product operations talent, actively develop their careers and build the next generation of Product Ops leaders
What Success Looks Like
We hold Product Ops leadership to a clear, outcome-oriented scorecard. You will know you are succeeding when:
<ul>
• PM Strategic Time Index improves across the cluster — PMs spend more time on strategy, research, and user engagement, and less on coordination overhead
• Product teams deliver more predictably with clear visibility of risks, dependencies, and progress
• Launches are smoother across agencies, with fewer last-minute issues, stronger adoption, and measurable reduction in post-launch incidents
• Product leaders have reliable operational and adoption insights, driven by trusted data, not anecdotes, to support strategic decisions
• Playbook Standardisation Rate improves — teams across agencies use shared playbooks and templates rather than reinventing processes each cycle
• Governance enables confidence without unnecessary overhead — lightweight, decision-enabling, not bureaucratic
• A high-performing, cross-agency Product Ops function is established with consistent standards, strong talent, and measurable citizen-facing impact
What We Are Looking For
<ul>
• Senior Operations Leadership: Proven ability to design, implement, and embed product operations frameworks across multiple agencies or portfolios at scale

• Pit Crew Leader Mindset: You understand that your job is to make the whole system win — building enabling infrastructure, not owning the product. You measure your success by how much better PMs can do their job
• Data-Driven Thinking: Advanced fluency in product analytics, metrics framework design, and insight generation — and the ability to build a culture where data shapes decisions at every level
• Systems Thinking: Demonstrated capability to design scalable solutions that work across complex, multi-agency environments without creating unnecessary process overhead
• Stakeholder Leadership: Strong ability to influence and align diverse stakeholders — from product teams to executive partners — around operational improvements and strategic direction
• Organisational Navigation: Comfort operating within government and public-sector constraints, including procurement, policy, inter-agency dynamics, and consensus-building norms
• People Leadership: Passion for developing high-performing teams, mentoring senior talent, and building collaborative Product Ops communities of practice across GovTech
• Strategic Mindset: Ability to connect operational excellence to broader product strategy and citizen value — not just execution, but impact at scale
Education
<ul>
• Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Information Systems, Engineering, or related fields
• Master's degree preferred in Business Administration (MBA), Information Systems, or Operations Management
Experience
<ul>
• 10+ years of professional experience in product operations, operations management, or delivery roles
• Demonstrated senior leadership across multiple product portfolios or agencies, with a track record of building and scaling high-performing operational functions
• Proven ability to design and implement scalable processes, governance frameworks, and operational standards with cross-agency impact
• Experience in product-focused, agile, or technology-driven environments
• Background in educational technology or government digital services is advantageous
Technical Competencies
<ul>
• Advanced proficiency in data analysis and visualisation tools (SQL, Python, Tableau, or similar)
• Strong understanding of agile methodologies, modern delivery toolchains, and product development workflows
• Expertise in operational metrics framework design and insight generation

GovTech, as the lead agency for Singapore's Smart Nation initiative, is seeking an Assistant Director for Programme Management within its Developer Productivity and Services (DPS) division. This role is crucial for overseeing and integrating two key programs: Developer Productivity, which enhances government engineers' coding and deployment processes, and Developer Services, focused on building a Central Product Marketplace for GovTech's offerings. The Assistant Director will ensure coherent execution across both programs, provide clear leadership visibility, and manage projects to translate strategies into actionable plans and measurable objectives. A significant part of the role involves driving the supply side of the Central Product Marketplace by engaging with over 45 GovTech platform product teams to integrate them onto the Console platform, requiring strong relationship management and judgment.
What you will own:

The programme management function across Developer Productivity and Developer Services, ensuring tight execution and conditions that make good product decisions possible. You will be responsible for managing projects within the programme, and play a leading role in nudging the teams to translate strategies into plans, OKRs reviewed with accountability, workstreams visible, blockers surfaced early, and the right people in the room when decisions need to be made. On the Developer Services side, a significant part of this is driving the supply side of the Central Product Marketplace, managing structured engagement sessions with 45+ GovTech platform product teams to get them integrated onto Console. This is a sustained, relationship driven effort that requires persistence, good judgment, and the ability to build trust across a wide group of stakeholders.
You are expected to:

Own the operating rhythm of both programmes, including strategy reviews, OKR cycles, and workstream tracking, to ensure teams focus on building. Maintain a clear line of sight across all active workstreams and flag risks early. Build and sustain working relationships with senior stakeholders, facilitating decisions that teams on the ground cannot make alone. Coach and mentor direct and indirect repor9ts, investing in team capability and creating an environment for optimal performance. Manage the small programme support team covering Procurement, Finance, and Admin, aligning these functions with programme priorities. Support the supply side Console integration effort through structured engagement sessions, removing blockers, tracking progress, and building a repeatable playbook.
You do this by:

Ensuring programme practices are lean and purposeful, such as regular workstream check ins, OKR reviews, and strategy sessions that surface information without creating meeting overhead. Staying close enough to each workstream to understand realities versus optimism without becoming a bottleneck. Enabling structured engagement with central product teams to sustain Console integration, building relationships, resolving hesitations, and making integration the path of least resistance. Working alongside PMs, designers, engineers, and product ops as a connector and enabler, understanding each discipline to ask the right questions and foster communication. Preparing leadership updates and briefings that are honest about status and clear about needed decisions. Building a high trust environment where the team raises issues early and collaborates to resolve them.
[What we are looking for]
Who we are looking for:

A programme manager skilled at making organizations work, not just tracking them. Candidates should have 8 to 14 years in programme or delivery management, ideally in technology, with a proven track record of coordinating complex, multi workstream portfolios across diverse teams. The ideal candidate works naturally with PMs, designers, engineers, and product ops, understanding each discipline to be a credible partner. They build strong stakeholder relationships, communicate clearly, and possess working knowledge of OKRs and performance frameworks, using data for accountability. Comfort in an AI assisted work environment and curiosity about technology trends are valued. Familiarity with developer facing platforms, government digital products, or large scale platform adoption is an advantage.
Why join us:

Work at the center of two of GovTech's most strategically important programmes, one reshaping how government engineers build software and the other building the marketplace for central products. Experience real scale and visibility, as the work impacts every agency developer and administrator in the Singapore Government. Gain direct access to senior leadership and a genuine seat at the table on programme direction. Join a team that values craft, comprising strong PMs, designers, and engineers who are serious about their work and seek a programme function that enhances their capabilities. About TradeNet

TradeNet is Singapore’s National Single Window for trade permit processing. It processes over 9 million permit applications annually across import, export and transshipment. As one of Singapore’s key trade systems, TradeNet is being brought in-house to strengthen technology ownership and long-term sustainability.
How we build

Designated as critical IT infrastructure, we favor simple, durable technology choices over the latest trends. We prioritize systems that are easy to reason about, operate, and maintain for the long term.

We operate with high autonomy. Engineers are expected to think deeply, exercise sound judgement, and take ownership of technical decisions. You own the code from technical design through to production. We practice and value honest feedback, practical decision-making and real impact.
What you'll do

The Data Practice drives innovation and sets best practices for the effective and responsible use of data across the Whole-of-Government (WOG). We work at the intersection of data engineering, AI, privacy, and governance - developing standards, platforms, and tools that enable agencies to build high-quality data products and unlock the value of data for public good.

A core focus of our work is advancing responsible data use. As data sharing and AI adoption accelerate, we develop both the frameworks and technologies needed to ensure sensitive data can be used safely; including in AI systems, where interactions with sensitive data are becoming more widespread and risks will scale further with more autonomous, agentic workflows.

A core focus of our work is to make responsible data use practical and scalable. This includes developing technical guardrails, privacy-preserving workflows, evaluation methods, and reusable standards that help agencies use data safely for analytics, AI, and digital services. Our work spans areas such as AI privacy, context-aware anonymisation, synthetic data generation, federated AI / computing, encrypted computation, differential privacy, and confidential computing. We bridge the gap between policy, research, and real-world deployment by experimenting with new approaches, validating them through agency pilots, and operationalising them into standards, implementation guides, and central government tools.

The Communications and Marketing Group (CMG) leads GovTech Singapore’s corporate, product, digital, social, media and internal communications. CMG builds public understanding and trust in GovTech’s work, supports adoption of digital government services, and strengthens GovTech’s reputation as a leading applied technology organisation in Singapore and internationally.

We are looking for a Deputy Director to join CMG’s leadership team. Working closely with the Director, CMG, the Deputy Director will lead teams across CMG, guide team leads, drive the group’s strategic priorities, strengthen operating discipline, and ensure high-quality communications support across GovTech.

This leadership role requires strong communications judgement, people leadership and the ability to work across complex and sensitive issues. The Deputy Director will partner senior management, product and engineering teams, policy stakeholders, parent ministry colleagues and external partners to shape clear, credible and effective communications for GovTech’s work.

You will lead teams within CMG and guide team leads across strategic communications, product communications, media relations, digital and social media, marketing communications, internal communications and issues management.
Your key responsibilities include:
<ul>
• Lead team leads and managers to develop integrated communications and marketing strategies for key GovTech products, platforms and services.
• Provide strategic communications counsel to senior management, division heads and project teams on positioning, messaging, stakeholder engagement and public communications risks.
• Guide teams in the planning and execution of media, digital, social, content, creative, events and outreach efforts to support product adoption, public awareness and corporate reputation.
• Co-lead issues management and crisis communications for incidents involving GovTech, including the development of holding lines, media replies, stakeholder messages and communications plans.
• Strengthen GovTech’s media engagement strategy, including relationships with local and international media, industry commentators, advocates and relevant opinion leaders.
• Work with the parent ministry and Smart Nation partners to align GovTech’s communications with broader national digital government and Smart Nation priorities.
• Support internal communications, including leadership messaging, organisational announcements and staff engagement on key GovTech priorities.
• Build team capability by coaching communications professionals, setting quality standards, improving operating processes and ensuring strong execution across multiple portfolios.
• Serve as senior communications lead for selected strategic portfolios, including GovTech’s cybersecurity-related communications and branding needs.
<ul>
• A degree in Mass Communications, Marketing, Public Relations, Journalism, Political Science, Public Policy or a related field.
• At least 12 years of experience in communications, media, marketing, public affairs or a related field, including at least five years in a leadership or managerial role.
• Strong strategic communications judgement, with the ability to shape clear narratives, advise senior leaders and manage complex stakeholder environments.
• Proven experience leading integrated communications campaigns across media, digital, social, content, events and marketing channels.
• Strong issues and crisis communications experience, including the ability to operate calmly and effectively in sensitive or fast-moving situations.
• Demonstrated experience leading and developing teams, including senior communications professionals and team leads.
• Excellent writing, editing and presentation skills, with the ability to translate complex technology, policy or organisational issues into clear public-facing messages.
• Strong understanding of the media and communications landscape, including digital and social media trends, public sentiment and reputation management.
• Experience cultivating and maintaining relationships with local and/or international media.
• Ability to work effectively with technical teams, policy teams, senior management and external partners.
• Understanding of the technology sector, public sector or digital government is an advantage, but not mandatory.
GovTech is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive workplace that values diverse voices and perspectives, as we believe that diversity is the foundation to innovation.

Our employee benefits are based on a total rewards approach, offering a holistic and market-competitive suite of perks. These include leave benefits to meet your work-life needs and employee wellness programs.
We champion flexible work arrangements (subject to your job role) and trust that you will manage your own time to deliver your best, wherever you are, and whatever works best for you.

Role Purpose

The Deputy Director (DD), Government Incident Reporting Ops, leads a high-performing operational team responsible for centralizing, assessing, and managing the full spectrum of Whole-of-Government (WOG) incident reports across all Singapore Government agencies.

The scope of coverage is multi-disciplinary, encompassing cybersecurity/data incidents, physical security breaches, public-facing service disruptions, and general operational failures. The DD ensures swift severity assessment, accurate fact-gathering, and seamless leadership escalation, while driving a WOG continuous learning culture to prevent systemic recurrence.
Key Responsibilities
Multi-Domain Operational Leadership
<ul>
• Lead daily operations for the WOG Incident Reporting framework, ensuring all submissions across cyber, physical, and operational domains are triaged and validated accurately.
<ul>
• Demonstrate sharp acumen to make critical judgment calls on complex, multi-domain incidents, ensuring appropriate escalation and containment strategies are triggered according to SOPs.
<ul>
• Review and refine high-quality, high-stakes incident summaries and assessments for senior leadership presentation under tight timelines.
Process Optimization & Culture Building
<ul>
• Drive continuous improvement initiatives to streamline the reporting workflow, leveraging technology to make reporting frictionless and encourage timely submissions from all agencies.
<ul>
• Foster a ""Just Culture"" across the public service, prioritizing psychological safety so agencies report incidents transparently without fear of blame.
WOG Knowledge Management & Continuous Learning
<ul>
• Transform diverse incident data into actionable insights, identifying trends and cross-domain vulnerabilities.
<ul>
• Develop effective mechanisms (e.g., cross-agency sharing sessions, post-incident reviews, systemic playbooks) to ensure lessons are institutionalized WOG.
Talent Development
<ul>
• Mentor and develop team officers, uplifting their technical literacy across different incident domains and honing their analytical capabilities.
Requirements & Qualifications
Technical & Domain Knowledge (Critical)
<ul>

• Cross-Domain Literacy: Strong foundational knowledge across IT infrastructure, Cybersecurity operations, and Physical Security frameworks. Must be able to speak the language of both tech engineers and physical security teams.
<ul>
• Incident Triage Expertise: Familiarity with incident classification models, threat landscapes, and standard risk matrix frameworks across both digital and physical environments.
Professional Experience
<ul>
• Experience in Large-Scale Operations: At least 8 years of professional experience managing complex operations, incident response, crisis management, or operational risk.
<ul>

• Organizational Scale: Proven track record of navigating and operating effectively within large, complex organizations (e.g., Multi-National Corporations (MNCs), major financial institutions, critical infrastructure operators, or public sector agencies).
<ul>
• Stakeholder Management: Demonstrated ability to manage diverse, high-level stakeholders and navigate matrixed organizational structures or multi-party ecosystems.
<ul>

• Public Sector Familiarity (Preferred but not mandatory): Prior experience within the Singapore Public Service, or a strong conceptual understanding of Whole-of-Government (WOG) governance structures and inter-agency dynamics, is highly advantageous. Private sector candidates with a strong adaptability to public sector governance are welcome to apply.
<ul>
• Process Improvement: Experience in operations design or process optimization (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma, Agile) to simplify reporting workflows and drive efficiency.
Critical Skills & Competencies
<ul>

• Executive Communication: Exceptional command of written and spoken English. Ability to translate highly technical, ambiguous, or complex incidents (like a zero-day exploit or a complex supply-chain failure) into concise, plain-language briefs for senior management.
<ul>
• High-Stakes Diplomacy: Ability to manage sensitive conversations with senior agency leaders, challenging an agency’s self-assessment firmly but tactfully to ensure proper treatment.
<ul>
• Data Analytics & Pattern Recognition: Ability to look beyond individual incidents to identify systemic clusters or root causes across the government ecosystem.
Key Personal Attributes
<ul>
• Mental Agility & Resilience: Thrives in a high-pressure, fast-paced environment where variables change rapidly during concurrent crises.
<ul>
• Emotional Intelligence (EQ): Essential for building trust with stressed reportees during an ongoing incident.
<ul>
• Uncompromising Integrity: Absolute discretion in handling highly sensitive, restricted, or politically charged information.

As the Centre of Excellence for Infocomm Technology and Smart Systems (ICT & SS), GovTech develops the Singapore Government’s capabilities in Data Science & Artificial Intelligence, Application Development, Smart City Technology, Digital Infrastructure, and Cybersecurity.

The challenge

What happens when technology, delivery and threats move faster than an organisation’s ability to see and respond to risk?

And what could become possible if risk management moved just as quickly?

Every organisation needs a way to detect warning signs, connect the dots and act before problems spread.

That is the role of governance, risk and control.

Think of it as the organisation’s nervous system. It picks up signals from across the organisation, helps leaders make sense of them and enables a timely response.

When that system works well, teams can move faster, take smarter risks and deliver with greater confidence. When it does not, warning signs are missed, decisions slow down and governance becomes a barrier rather than an enabler.

GovTech has strong platforms, talented people and an important mission. As our role and public impact grow, the risks we manage are becoming more interconnected, fast-moving and consequential.

We are looking for Deputy Directors and Assistant Directors in Enterprise Risk Management who want to help build what comes next.

You will have the opportunity to challenge established practices, experiment with data and AI, influence senior decisions and shape how one of Singapore’s most important technology organisations manages risk.
This is a role for people who want more than a steady portfolio. It is for those who want to build, push boundaries and leave the system better than they found it.
What you will have the chance to change. We want to move enterprise risk management:
<ul>
<li>
from periodic reporting to more continuous risk visibility
<li>
from manual collation to data and AI-enabled insight
<li>
from risk registers to clearer decisions and action
<li>
from unclear accountability to risks with active owners
<li>
from retrospective assurance to earlier intervention
<li>
from compliance activity to practical support for delivery
This is not simply a reporting role. You will help shape how risk is understood, discussed, owned and acted upon across GovTech.
Your mandate
Your job is to make enterprise risk management useful.
You will work with senior leaders, risk owners and teams across GovTech to identify what matters, make trade-offs visible and support action before issues become incidents.
Depending on your experience and appointment level, you will lead or take ownership of significant ERM portfolios and initiatives.

You will have room to test ideas, challenge established practices and build better approaches. You will also need to influence people you do not manage and create clarity where risks, priorities or accountabilities are contested.
That is part of the job.
Break the Frame
Modern risk management cannot rely only on inherited frameworks, templates and periodic reporting.
We want people who are prepared to question established practices, test better approaches and rethink how risk management should work in a technology organisation.
You will explore how data, AI and automation can help GovTech:
<ul>
<li>
detect weak signals and emerging risks earlier
<li>
connect information across the organisation
<li>
reduce manual reporting and administrative work
<li>
give leaders more timely and useful risk insight
<li>
strengthen judgement without removing human accountability
This requires an experimental mindset. You should be comfortable testing ideas, learning from what does not work and turning successful experiments into practical capabilities.
The aim is not to use AI to perform old processes faster. It is to ask whether those processes are still needed and design better ones where they are not.
We call this Break the Frame: looking beyond established ways of working, pushing boundaries responsibly and building an ERM function that can keep pace with modern technology.
What you will do
Strengthen our ERM approach
Develop and improve GovTech’s enterprise risk framework, methodology and governance arrangements.
Clarify who owns each risk, how issues should be escalated and where decisions should sit.
Make sure the approach works for a modern technology organisation rather than forcing teams into processes that add little value.
Build a forward-looking view of risk
Maintain a current view of GovTech’s key risks across strategy, technology, operations, delivery, vendors, regulation, data, reputation and organisational capability.
Look beyond known issues and past incidents. Identify emerging threats, dependencies and concentrations of risk before they become larger problems.
Keep GovTech’s enterprise risk profile, register and monitoring approach relevant and useful to decision-makers.
Support better leadership decisions
Provide clear and practical advice to senior leadership, Board-level committees, auditors and oversight bodies, including SNDGO and relevant central agencies.
Turn complex risk issues into straightforward choices, trade-offs and recommendations.

• Systems thinking across business, technology, and risk.

You will begin with an intensive three to six months training programme under our experienced IT Audit Shared Services Central team in GovTech, where you will build essential skills before taking on IT Audit Officer role at AGO.

Government Commercial Cloud (GCC) is a key platform within Singapore Government Technology Stacks that enables government agencies to build and operate digital services on commercial cloud. The GCC Engineering team develops platform automations, landing zones, and security tooling across AWS, Azure, and GCP — serving thousands of government systems and thousands of public officers.
Security at GCC is not a side function — it's core to the platform's value proposition. Government agencies trust GCC to be secure by default.

You are the single named owner of security outcomes across all engineering teams in GCC. You define how security works — the standards, processes, escalation paths, and technical approaches — and drive adoption through influence, not authority. You operate through a Security Champions network: persistent, named engineers in each product team who own security judgment locally, coordinated by you. Your accountability is whether GCC is actually secure — measured through process health, incident response quality, and security posture metrics you define.

This role is part of the organisation's domain leadership structure — you join alongside Engineering Managers as a peer, not as a report to any EM. The Security domain is being stood up fresh. The previous model (centralised security team gatekeeping all decisions) has been retired. You inherit a Champions network in early stages, documented runbooks, and interim coverage from a senior security advisor. Your job is to take it from ""interim bridge"" to ""sustainable, scalable security function.""

The domain scope will evolve. Today it centres on the areas listed above — but we expect the role to grow into adjacent areas (AI security, detection engineering) as the organisation's needs develop. Adaptability and willingness to define your own frontier matters more than deep expertise in every area on day one.
Security Architecture & Posture
<ul>
• Own the organisation's security posture across all product teams and cloud environments
• Architect security frameworks that integrate into engineering workflows without creating bottlenecks
• Design and evolve threat modelling methodologies adapted to the organisation's multi-cloud, multi-tenant context
• Define escalation paths, severity frameworks, and incident response playbooks
• Own the relationship with GCSOC, shaping how external security signals translate into internal action
• Drive security tooling strategy — selecting, configuring, and setting alert thresholds that distinguish signal from noise
Standards & Process Design
<ul>
• Define security standards, runbooks, and compliance approaches that teams can self-serve against
• Design the Security Champions model: training curriculum, forum cadence, escalation criteria, and what ""good"" looks like for a champion
• Replace gatekeeping with enablement — move from ""security reviews everything"" to ""teams self-certify against clear criteria, you spot-check and consult""
• Own security decision records: all posture choices documented, auditable, and transferable
• Reform compliance processes (e.g. IMR8) to reduce ceremony while maintaining assurance
Cross-Org Influence
<ul>
• Drive security adoption across 5-6 engineering teams through the Champions network
• Run a regular cross-org security forum: shared learning, emerging threats, pattern reviews
• Consult on high-risk designs and architectural trade-offs when teams escalate
• Handle genuine security incidents personally, with Champions as informed participants
• Build security judgment across the engineering organisation — not by centralising decisions, but by raising the floor

• Serve as the organisation's authoritative security voice on technical matters — advising on vendor evaluations, platform-level policy design, and cross-programme security decisions that require deep domain expertise beyond any single team's scope
Technical Depth
<ul>
• Maintain hands-on capability in at least two of: cloud security architecture, application security, supply chain security, detection engineering
• Evaluate and prototype security tooling; make build-vs-buy recommendations grounded in the org's actual threat model
• Contribute to or lead security incident post-mortems with root cause analysis that drives systemic improvement
• Stay current on emerging threats and translate external signals into organisational action
Must-Have
<ul>
• Deep security engineering expertise (architecture, not just operations) — you've designed security frameworks, not just followed them
• Demonstrated ability to influence without authority across multiple engineering teams
• Experience designing security processes that scale through enablement rather than gatekeeping
• Strong enough as an engineer to review designs, read code, and earn credibility with senior SWEs
• Clear, structured communication — you'll write strategies, runbooks, and decision records that outlive you
• Comfort operating with ambiguity: this role is being stood up for the first time, and you'll shape what it becomes
• Proficiency in scripting (Python, Bash) and working with APIs — you'll build and review automation, not just specify it
• Solid understanding of identity, networking, logging, monitoring, and data security in cloud environments
Strong Signals
<ul>
• Experience with cloud security across multiple CSPs — ideally hands-on with native security services, not just console-level familiarity
• Background in both offensive (threat modelling, VAPT, red team) and defensive (SIEM, detection engineering, incident response) security
• Track record of building security champion or embedded security programs
• Experience with CNAPP/CSPM platforms and vulnerability management tooling
• Experience integrating security controls into CI/CD pipelines and DevSecOps workflows
• Familiarity with compliance and threat frameworks and the judgment to know when compliance ≠ security
• Experience working in government or highly regulated environments
• Awareness of AI security risks and emerging governance frameworks
Technology Landscape
You'll encounter the following in this role. We don't expect mastery of all of these on day one — what matters is the ability to learn quickly and form sound judgment across unfamiliar tools.
| Area | Technologies |
| Cloud providers | AWS, Azure, GCP (multi-account/subscription/project at scale) |
| Security posture | Wiz, AWS Security Hub, Azure Defender, GCP Security Command Center |
| Vulnerability management | Nessus, Trivy, AWS Inspector, container scanning |
| SIEM & detection | Elastic SIEM, GuardDuty, Sentinel, CloudTrail/Activity Log |
| Identity & access | IAM (all CSPs), Entra ID, workload identity, RBAC/ABAC patterns |
| IaC & pipelines | Terraform, GitLab CI/CD, policy-as-code (OPA, Sentinel) |
| Secrets & supply chain | Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, SBOM tooling, dependency scanning |
| Compliance frameworks | IMR8, CIS Benchmarks, NIST CSF, ISO 27001, MITRE ATT&CK |
| Scripting & automation | Python, Bash, REST APIs |
| Emerging | AI/LLM security (OWASP LLM Top 10, NIST AI RMF), detection-as-code |
Preferred Certifications
Not required, but signal depth in relevant areas:
<ul>
• Cloud security: AWS Security Specialty, Azure Security Engineer Associate, GCP Professional Cloud Security Engineer
• Security generalist: CISSP, CCSP, or relevant GIAC certifications
• Offensive: OSCP, GPEN, or equivalent hands-on security testing credentials
Dealbreakers
<ul>
• Pure compliance/audit background with no engineering depth — this role requires technical credibility with senior engineers
• Preference for centralised control (""everything goes through security"") — the operating model is distributed enablement
• Inability to document and codify decisions — if you leave, someone else must be able to pick up without an information gap

At Singpass, we aim to provide reliable digital identity for Singapore that streamlines transactions, enables businesses, and protects against fraud.
