What you will be working on:
As an Lead Cybersecurity Engineer, your job will be to:
<ul>
• Determine what assurance gaps exist across our product portfolio and decide what assessment approaches best surface real risk and drive meaningful remediation
• Shape the strategic direction of our cybersecurity assurance programme and prioritise activities based on the threat landscape, product criticality, and organisational risk appetite
• Work with people from engineering, product, policy, and operations to ensure security assurance is embedded as a rigorous and trusted function across our digital services
• Measure and track the effectiveness of our assurance activities, from assessment coverage and finding severity trends to remediation rates and compliance posture

• Wear multiple hats to keep our systems honest. You may be leading a penetration test, conducting a secure architecture review, facilitating a threat modelling exercise, or advising on a governance/risk/compliance matter
• Build a culture of accountability and continuous improvement with the people you work with
What we are looking for

We are looking for someone who can independently lead a credible and effective assurance function that gives the organisation confidence in the security of its products and practices, and who can operate effectively across a complex, multi-product environment.
In this role, you will:
<ul>

• Own and drive assurance impact across the digital identity space
    Take end-to-end ownership of the cybersecurity assurance function across our product portfolio, shaping direction in alignment with Singpass' broader security strategy. Translate risk priorities, regulatory requirements, and product roadmaps into a coherent assurance programme that delivers clear, actionable findings and measurable improvements in security posture.

• Lead rigorous security testing across a complex, multi-product environment
    Own the end-to-end approach to various security testing engagements across the division. Bring deep hands-on expertise to bear in planning, scoping, executing, and reviewing engagements — ensuring findings are technically sound, well-evidenced, and tied to real-world risk.

• Drive secure architecture reviews and threat modelling
    Lead structured reviews of system and application architectures to identify security weaknesses before they are built in. Facilitate threat modelling exercises with engineering and product teams, ensuring that security risks are surfaced early and addressed systematically across the product lifecycle.

• Make high-quality, risk-informed decisions
    Define assurance metrics, evaluate trade-offs, and prioritise activities effectively using vulnerability data, architecture assessments, and strategic context. Focus efforts on the assessments and findings that drive the most meaningful risk reduction across a broad and evolving attack surface.

• Bring structure and credibility to cyber GRC
    Apply working knowledge of cybersecurity governance, risk, and compliance to ensure our assurance activities align with relevant frameworks, regulations, and internal policies. Help the organisation maintain a well-documented, defensible security posture and support audit and compliance processes with rigour and clarity.

• Demonstrated experience leading cybersecurity assurance functions or teams and driving assurance programmes end-to-end
• Proven hands-on expertise in conducting and overseeing penetration testing and vulnerability assessments across complex, multi-product or multi-service environments
• Experience leading secure architecture reviews and threat modelling exercises, with a track record of surfacing meaningful risk early in the product lifecycle
• Possess the OSCP certification, or other equivalent or advanced certifications
• Working knowledge of cybersecurity GRC, including familiarity with relevant frameworks such as IM8, NIST CSF, or equivalent
• Experience working closely with software engineering and product teams to translate assurance findings into remediation outcomes

Candidate must possess strong log analysis and digital forensics skills to drive effective responses to cybersecurity incidents that ensure secure delivery of applications and infrastructure services. <ul>
• Application logs
<ul>

<ul>
• Endpoint systems and servers
<ul>
• Network devices and logs
<ul>
• Cloud environments
<ul>

<ul>

<ul>

As a Lead Product Manager, you will shape the strategy and roadmap of the fCMS. This role is not about managing a fixed set of requirements. It is about helping the Judiciary modernise critical systems in a way that delivers value incrementally, reduces delivery risk and creates long-term adaptability. You will help the platform respond to new legislation, policies and judicial processes, while improving the experience of those who use and operate the courts.
Shape the future of justice in Singapore

Justice is one of Singapore's most important public services. Every year, almost 200,000 cases pass through our courts, involving individuals, families, businesses, lawyers and public agencies. Behind every case is someone seeking a fair, timely and accessible resolution.

The Judiciary's transformation into One Judiciary brought together the Supreme Court, State Courts and Family Justice Courts under a shared vision of delivering justice that is trusted, accessible and ready for the future.
Realising this vision requires more than organisational change. It requires rethinking the digital systems, processes and services that underpin how justice is delivered.

The Future Courts Management System (fCMS) is the Judiciary's flagship digital transformation programme, developed in close partnership with GovTech. You will join GovTech's product management community while working deeply with the Judiciary to shape products that support the administration of justice across Singapore's Courts.

This is not simply a like-for-like replacement of legacy systems. It is an opportunity to reimagine how court services should work: making them easier to use, more responsive to changing legislation and policies, and better able to serve everyone who depends on them.
This is a rare opportunity to help shape how justice will be delivered in Singapore for years to come.
In this role, you will:
<ul>
<li>
Shape product strategy for fCMS domains, translating Judiciary priorities, user needs, operational complexity and legislative changes into clear roadmaps and measurable outcomes.
<li>
Work in a product trio with Engineering and Design leads to discover, prioritise and deliver solutions that are valuable, usable, feasible, secure and scalable.
<li>

Understand users and court operations by working with judges, judicial officers, lawyers, court administrators, partner agencies and members of the public to identify where digital products can make the greatest difference.
<li>
Deliver value incrementally using modern product and engineering practices that reduce delivery risk, support learning from real usage and avoid big-bang replacement.
<li>
Shape a secure and adaptable platform that can support evolving court processes, new government policies, integrations, data needs and long-term operational resilience.
<li>
Build alignment and product capability by communicating product direction clearly, influencing through evidence, and coaching or guiding Product Managers where appropriate.
You'll Thrive in This Role If...
<ul>
<li>
You bring clarity to ambiguity — framing complex user, operational, legal and policy problems into clear product opportunities.
<li>
You think strategically and systemically — understanding how court processes, technology, legislation, data and organisational change connect across One Judiciary.
<li>
You make thoughtful product trade-offs — balancing user value, operational needs, technical sustainability, security, compliance and delivery risk.
<li>
You lead through influence — building alignment across senior stakeholders, court operations, legal, policy, design, engineering and technology partners.
<li>

You are comfortable with modern digital delivery — working with multidisciplinary teams, Agile delivery, cloud platforms, APIs, integrations, enterprise systems, product analytics and secure-by-design practices.
<li>

You raise the bar for product practice — coaching Product Managers where appropriate, contributing to GovTech's product community and strengthening a culture of discovery, evidence and continuous improvement.

Experience leading complex digital products, platforms or enterprise workflows is important. Experience in government, justice, regulated environments or large-scale transformation programmes will be advantageous, but not essential.

In this role, you will help the Judiciary:
<ul>
<li>
Improve access to justice by shaping digital services that are easier to use, more inclusive and better aligned to the needs of court users.
<li>
Modernise critical court operations by streamlining workflows across courts, case types and user groups.
<li>
Respond faster to change by enabling new legislation, policies and judicial processes to be implemented more quickly and consistently.

Build a resilient, adaptable platform that is secure, scalable and able to evolve with the Judiciary's long-term needs.

Why This Role Is Different
Few product management roles offer the opportunity to redesign digital systems that underpin an entire national institution.

As part of GovTech, you will bring modern product, design and engineering practices to one of the Judiciary's most important transformation programmes. As part of the fCMS, you will help shape how justice is delivered in Singapore — not just by building better technology, but by helping create a Judiciary that is more accessible, more responsive and better prepared for the future.

• Provide regular portfolio reporting to the CIO (progress, risks, budget, benefits, adoption), and drive timely resolution of cross-team blockers.

<li>
Ensure that data consumers can assess dataset fitness-for-purpose directly within the discovery experience, without needing to contact data owners separately

Job Summary

GovTech is seeking a strategic and mission-driven Lead/Senior Product Manager to spearhead the AI Safety and Governance pillar within PlatformAI. As AI adoption scales across the public sector, your mission is to ensure that every AI-enabled application is secure, fair, and accountable by design.
You will own a dual-track roadmap:
<ul>
• For Developers: Building the ""Safety Stack""—a suite of automated Evals, Guardrails, and Red-teaming tools that allow teams to deploy LLMs with speed and confidence.
<ul>

• For Governance and Observability: Architecting the ""Governance Layer""—observability tools and risk-posture dashboards that provide a unified view of AI compliance across the whole-of-government (WOG) ecosystem.
Key Responsibilities
1. Defining the Sovereign Safety Standard
<ul>
• Define the long-term strategy for AI Safety-as-a-Service, transitioning governance from a manual checklist to an automated platform feature.
• Synthesize emerging global frameworks and local AI governance policies into platform features that make compliance ""invisible"" for developers.
• Establish the government’s standard for AI risk levels, determining the safety benchmarks required for different use cases (e.g., citizen-facing vs. internal productivity).
2. Building the Guardrails & Audit Trails
<ul>
• Lead the development of automated evaluation engines that stress-test products and models for prompt injection, PII leakage, toxicity, and hallucination before and after deployment.
• Partner with Engineering to integrate safety checks directly into CI/CD pipelines, ensuring that ""Safety-by-Design"" accelerates rather than hinders deployment.
• Build real-time monitoring tools to detect ""jailbreak"" attempts and model drift, ensuring rapid mitigation of live AI risks.
3. Bridging Policy & Code
<ul>
• Act as the primary liaison between Policy/Legal teams and Engineering teams to ensure technical tools meet policy and legal intent.
• Cultivate a culture of safety across GovTech by publishing playbooks, standardizing red-teaming exercises, and educating teams on the evolving LLM vulnerability landscape.
4. Trust-Centric Metrics & Accountability
<ul>
• Define and track KPIs such as Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) vulnerabilities, Policy Coverage %, and Guardrail Efficacy Rates.
What You Will Bring
<ul>
• Senior Product Leadership: Proven experience managing complex technical products, specifically those focused on Security, Governance, or AI/ML infrastructure.
<ul>
• AI Safety Domain Expertise: Deep understanding of Generative AI risks (e.g., prompt injection, training data poisoning, algorithmic bias) and the current state of AI safety research.
<ul>
• The ""Translator"" Skillset: Exceptional ability to distil abstract ethical principles into concrete technical requirements and APIs.
<ul>
• Analytical Rigor: A background in using data-driven evaluation frameworks (e.g., RAG evaluation, perplexity scoring, or model benchmarking) to measure performance and risk.
<ul>
• Developer Empathy: A deep understanding of developer workflows and a commitment to making safety tools an ""accelerant"" rather than a ""roadblock.""

The DV module is a centralised, reusable document verification capability built within the Work Pass Integrated System (WINS). It consolidates what was previously fragmented verification logic spread across independent systems for Employment Pass, S Pass, Work Permit, and Migrant Domestic Worker applications into a single, shared module.

The key goals of the module are to eliminate duplication of verification workflows and maintenance effort, standardise and harmonise DV processes across pass types, and enable verified documents to be shared across applications so that applicants do not need to resubmit the same documents for different pass types. This improves efficiency for both MOM officers processing applications and applicants going through the work pass application journey.
Understanding and Defining Requirements

Product Ops is responsible for deeply understanding the current state of Document Verification across the various pass types and documenting the pain points — such as duplicated verification logic, workflow discrepancies, and the need for applicants to resubmit the same documents across different pass applications. They translate these into clear, structured business and functional requirements for the centralised DV module, ensuring it meets the needs of all pass types without compromising on pass-type-specific rules or validations.
Stakeholder Engagement and Alignment

Product Ops acts as the bridge between MOM policy owners, operations teams, and the technical development team. This involves facilitating workshops and interviews with stakeholders from each pass type domain to surface existing workflows, identify divergences, and agree on a common, harmonised process. Given that DV currently exists independently across multiple systems, managing stakeholder alignment and buy-in for a shared module is a significant part of the role.
Process Mapping and Gap Analysis

A core responsibility is mapping out the as-is DV workflows for each pass type and conducting a thorough gap analysis to identify where processes diverge and where they can be standardised. Product Ops would document these in process flow diagrams and use them to define the to-be state — a unified DV workflow that is flexible enough to accommodate pass-type-specific requirements while eliminating unnecessary duplication.
Defining the Shared Document Repository Logic

One of the key features of the new DV module is the ability to share verified documents across pass type applications, so applicants do not need to resubmit the same documents. Product Ops is responsible for defining the business rules around this — for example, what constitutes a valid previously verified document, how long a verified document remains valid, and under what conditions a document must be re-verified. These rules need to be clearly articulated before development begins.
User Stories and Acceptance Criteria

Product Ops translates requirements into well-defined user stories and acceptance criteria that the development team can work from. For a reusable module like DV, this includes stories covering document upload, verification workflows, document sharing logic, exception handling, and integration touchpoints with the various pass type systems.
Integration and Dependency Management

Since the DV module needs to integrate with multiple existing systems across the different pass types, Product Ops plays a key role in mapping out integration requirements and dependencies. This includes working with technical architects to understand API contracts, data flows, and how the centralised module will be consumed by each downstream system.
Supporting UAT and Change Management

Product Ops supports user acceptance testing by preparing test scenarios that cover the full range of pass types and document verification scenarios, including edge cases. They also play a role in change management — helping operations and policy teams understand how the new centralised module changes their workflows, and ensuring that training and communication materials accurately reflect the new processes.
Metrics and Success Criteria

Product Ops helps define what success looks like for the DV module — for instance, reduction in duplicate document submissions, reduction in maintenance overhead across systems, and improvement in processing time. Tracking these metrics post-launch also falls within the Product Ops remit, helping the team iterate and improve the module over time.

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field.
• Proven experience in software development, system analysis, or a similar technical role.
• Proficiency in at least one modern programming language (e.g., Java, Python, Go, C#).
• Experience with cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP) and containerization technologies (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes) is highly desirable.
• Strong understanding of database concepts and experience with SQL/NoSQL databases.
• Familiarity with API design and development principles.
• Excellent problem-solving, analytical, and critical thinking skills.
• Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with diverse stakeholders.
• Ability to work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced environment.

You develop operational strategies and work closely with cross-functional teams to deliver on product goals. At the senior level, you operate with high autonomy across a large or multi-product problem space — addressing complex, often unprecedented challenges, guiding others, and influencing practices beyond your immediate team. Target Portfolio Scope

You will support product operations within one or more assigned product areas in Rehabilitation & Protection Group (RPG) of MSF. Within this scope, you will partner closely with business owners and Product team on aligning standards and practices.

Organised across the 5 core pillars of Product Ops at RPG of MSF:
Strategic Partnership
<ul>

• Build trusted relationships across product, engineering, design, policy, and business owner teams, ensure alignment on operational priorities

Data-Driven Insights

• Champion the product intelligence infrastructure for your product area — dashboards, telemetry, feedback repositories and ensure insights are activated in decisions, not just displayed

• Own operational excellence in change communication and go-to-market execution for product launches, ensure users and schools are ready before go-live
• Establish and maintain best practices for feedback management and closed-loop resolution
Cross-Functional Orchestration

• Drive operational initiatives aligned to organisational goals, actively contribute to optimizing for growth

We are looking for a Product Ops specialist to support STARS2.0's Phase 2 delivery squads and the parallel discovery into the platform law firms use to submit property transactions. This role sits at the intersection of business analysis and product delivery: you will analyse existing business processes, translate business and regulatory requirements into clear product requirements, and help the delivery squads avoid simply replicating STARS1's existing business rules where those rules can instead be rationalised and simplified.
This is a forward-deployed role: you will be embedded within the Singapore Land Authority (SLA), working day-to-day alongside Registration Officers, business stakeholders, and the engineers, designers and Product Managers across both Phase 2 squads.
You will be shared across both delivery squads and into the parallel discovery workstream, giving you visibility into how requirements and business logic connect across the whole programme rather than being scoped to a single team's backlog.

About the programme
STARS2.0 is the programme to modernise STARS, Singapore's Land Titles Registry system, which has been in operation since 1993 and today manages approximately 2 million live titles. It is operationally critical infrastructure: it processes 500,000 property transactions a year and is the single source of truth by which the Government records and guarantees land ownership in Singapore.
STARS2.0 is not a standalone technology project. It sits at the centre of a wider Land Titles Registry transformation that extends beyond the registry itself - to the digital platform through which law firms submit property transactions, the Digital Conveyancing Portal, and adjacent systems. This role spans both the core registry modernisation and a parallel discovery into that wider ecosystem.

Business process analysis
You will analyse how STARS1's existing business processes and rules actually work today, identifying which are genuinely load-bearing regulatory logic and which are legacy implementation artefacts that can be simplified in STARS2.0. This is central to the programme's approach: STARS1's business rules were, in places, hardcoded for implementation convenience rather than reflecting the underlying regulation, and a key goal of STARS2.0 is to rationalise rather than replicate that logic.

Requirements translation
You will work with Registration Officers, policy stakeholders and Product Managers to translate business needs, operational realities and regulatory requirements into clear, actionable product requirements that engineering and design can build against. You will help ensure requirements are documented with enough precision that squads can build from defined criteria rather than discovering constraints mid-delivery.

Cross-squad and cross-track support

About the Role
We are looking for Product Designers who are problem solvers first.

Your role is to understand how they work, identify the right problems to solve, and design products and services that make their work simpler and more effective. You will work across: Problem Framing · Service Design · UX Design from discovery and validation through to build and continuous improvement.

• Understand users' workflows, information needs and decision-making processes.
• Turn research and insights into better product and service experiences.

Validate & Improve
<ul>
• Turn assumptions into hypotheses and prototypes that can be tested.
• Conduct concept and usability testing with users.
• Iterate based on qualitative and quantitative evidence.
• Stay involved during build to ensure the intended experience is delivered.
• Use user feedback, product usage and outcomes to continuously improve the product.

• Make complex problems understandable through clear visualisation and storytelling.

About Us
The Government Technology Agency (GovTech) builds technology for the public good to improve the lives of Singaporeans and support public agencies in driving digital transformation. Within GovTech, the Anti-Scam Products (GASP) division operates with a clear, critical mission: to build tech products to detect, disrupt, and deter scammers at scale.

Scams are a complex, multi-million-dollar threat, costing Singaporeans hundreds of millions annually. GASP stands at the forefront of this adversarial space, building Singapore’s digital shield. By shifting from manual, reactive triage to proactive, AI-enabled, ecosystem-wide disruption, we target high-traffic convergent points, such as malicious websites, online monikers, and phone lines, where the government has a scalable defender’s advantage.
The Role

We are seeking a highly driven and strategic Product Manager or Senior Product Manager to join our ranks. In this role, you will step into a fast-paced, high-stakes environment where your product decisions directly erode the Return on Investment (ROI) of transnational scam syndicates.

You will not be constrained to a single predefined path. Depending on the evolving threat landscape, you may take the helm of one of our mature, scaled systems, such as SATIS (our end-to-end scam analysis and intervention system), rMSE (our AI/ML site evaluator), or G.R.A.P.H (our relationship analytics hub). Alternatively, you may be tasked with the zero-to-one development of an entirely new anti-scam initiative to address emerging vulnerabilities.
Key Responsibilities
<ul>
<li>

Product Strategy & Vision: Own a product or feature area, driving its success from conception to launch. You will develop the product vision, align cross-functional teams around long-term goals, and define North Star success metrics to ensure your product delivers tangible public value.
<li>

Analytical & Product Sense: Operate in an ambiguous, fast-moving space by making critical decisions and prioritisations based on data. You will continuously evaluate features informed by user research, market trends, and internal feedback loops, leveraging data to validate or pivot ideas prior to development.
<li>

Execution & Delivery: Collaborate closely with software engineers, data scientists, and UX designers to balance speed, quality, and simplicity. You will foster a culture of agility, carefully navigating the short-term trade-offs of rapid deployment against long-term technical debt.
<li>

Stakeholder Orchestration: Act as a crucial liaison between business leadership, operational partners like the Singapore Police Force (SPF), and global tech platforms (e.g., Google, Meta). You will navigate disagreements constructively, facilitate WOG (Whole-of-Government) alignment, and drive systemic value across the organisation.
<li>

Mentorship & Leadership: Take full ownership of broad, ambiguously-scoped projects. You will synthesise complex data into clear strategic recommendations, proactively drive workstreams, and mentor junior team members to actively raise overall team capability and productivity.
What We Are Looking For
<ul>
<li>
Proven experience in product management, with a track record of independently owning assigned tasks or leading complex, end-to-end delivery of ambiguous projects.
<li>
Strong analytical intuition with the ability to identify and mitigate risks from both a technical and market perspective.
<li>
A profound sense of ownership to identify opportunities, recommend process improvements, and take calculated risks while learning from both successes and failures.
<li>

A commitment to collaborative growth: you proactively offer help, constructively challenge existing processes for continuous improvement, and share successes and failures openly to ensure team success.
If you are ready to apply your product craft to solve a billion-dollar problem and build tools that outmanoeuvre scams, join us at GASP. Together, we will build technology that protects Singaporeans.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company as we believe that diversity is meaningful to innovation. Our employee benefits are based on a total rewards approach, offering a holistic and market-competitive suite of perks. This includes generous leave benefits to meet your work-life needs. We trust that you will get the job done wherever you are, and whatever works best for you – so work from home or take a break to exercise if you need to*. We also believe it’s important for you to keep honing your craft in the constantly evolving tech landscape, so we provide and support a plethora of in-house and external learning and development opportunities all year round.

*Subject to the nature of your job role that might require you to be onsite during fixed hours

About ESTL
The Experimental Systems and Technology Lab (ESTL) is a GovTech engineering team embedded within the Ministry of Education (MOE). Find out more at https://www.estl.edu.sg/.

About All Ears
All Ears (AE) is MOE's data-collection platform, purpose-built around how MOE actually works. Since 2022 it has been adopted across 337 schools, where staff have created ~177,000 forms and logged over 11.5 million submissions. It does natively what commercial tools cannot without prohibitive per-seat costs: rostering, identity verification, response tracking, and deep integration with MOE's master data.

AE is now evolving from a forms tool into essential infrastructure, connecting information from the ground (students, parents, teachers) to decision-makers (school leaders, middle managers, HQ), with speed and minimal administrative effort. We win on merit: schools and HQ choose AE because it is genuinely better for their context, not because they are told to.

What you will be working on
As Senior Product Manager for All Ears, you will own the platform end-to-end and define its next chapter. All Ears has established itself across 337 schools and millions of submissions, adopted on merit rather than mandate, and its future direction remains deliberately open. You will be responsible for shaping it: identifying the highest-leverage opportunities, determining what the platform should become, and driving it there. The mandate is broad and ambiguously scoped by design, and you will pursue it at MOE's scale, where every decision compounds across millions of transactions and is felt directly in schools and classrooms.
Your responsibilities
<ul>
• Own All Ears’ vision and roadmap, taking full ownership of broad, ambiguously-scoped initiatives from discovery through delivery and operations.
• Identify high-impact problems and prioritise with discipline, using data to validate or kill ideas before development — and learn from both wins and misses.
• Be the expert on All Ears’ data: measure key metrics at least quarterly and use them to drive and defend product decisions.
• Ground decisions in user research, customer feedback, and market and competitor review, and mitigate product risks across technical and market dimensions.
• Foster a culture of speed, simplicity, and agility — weighing speed against long-term technical debt — and partner closely with engineers and designers to run disciplined, metric-driven delivery.
• Serve as the key liaison between HQ/business leadership and the product team, coordinating cross-functional collaboration and building alignment across stakeholders.
• Navigate disagreements constructively and challenge existing processes to drive improvement at the team and division level.
• Mentor junior team members and share successes and failures openly, reinforcing a strong learning culture.
What we are looking for
<ul>
• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field — or equivalent product experience.
• Proven track record in product management (typically 6+ years), with at least one complex product or platform delivered end-to-end.
• Strong strategic thinking, with the ability to turn ideas into shipped reality.
• Fluency in product discovery (user research, requirement analysis, prototyping), product lifecycle management, Agile/Scrum, stakeholder management, and roadmap planning.
• Strong data sense — comfortable using metrics to drive and defend product decisions.
• Excellent communication, able to translate fluidly between technical and business audiences.
• Experience mentoring or guiding more junior team members.
• A plus: experience with large-scale or high-volume platforms, internal-platform/extensibility models (SDKs/APIs), or the public-sector and education context.
• Overall, we look for people with ability, initiative, strong communication, and sound values — and who want their work to compound across an entire organisation.

As a Product Manager, you will be responsible for the end-to-end lifecycle of one or more digital products, shaping and delivering solutions that drive meaningful outcomes for the agency and its stakeholders.

You will define and manage product strategy and roadmaps aligned with organisational goals, working closely with cross-functional teams in engineering, design, and operations to deliver high-quality, user-centric products. Through research, user insights, and data analysis, you will identify opportunities, conceptualise features, and ensure successful and timely delivery of product releases. You will also define success metrics, monitor product performance, and continuously optimise features to maximise adoption and value.
<ul>
<li>

Define and drive product strategy and roadmap
Manage the product lifecycle end-to-end—from discovery and ideation to delivery and continuous improvement—ensuring alignment to organisational goals and user needs.
<li>

Lead product discovery and innovation
Conduct market research, user analysis, and trend assessments to identify opportunities, validate problem statements, and conceptualise impactful products and features.
<li>

Own product outcomes and delivery
Define clear success metrics, prioritise initiatives, and drive execution to deliver measurable impact and value.
<li>

Translate business and policy needs into product solutions
Scope requirements, develop user stories, and operationalise complex policy or business intent into scalable digital products.
<li>

Drive cross-functional collaboration and execution
Partner closely with engineering, design, product operations, and stakeholders to deliver high-quality products within budget and timelines.
<li>

Shape user-centric product experiences
Work with UX teams to design intuitive user journeys, ensuring coherent content, voice, and end-to-end experience.
<li>

Manage and prioritise the product backlog
Balance competing demands, make trade-offs, and ensure focus on highest-value features aligned with user and organisational outcomes.
<li>

Adopt data-driven decision making
Leverage data, user insights, and experimentation to inform prioritisation, monitor performance, and continuously improve products.
<li>

Drive go-to-market and product adoption strategies
Execute launch, adoption, and engagement plans to maximise product uptake and deliver strong value propositions to users and ecosystem partners.
<li>

Navigate complex stakeholder environments
Align across agencies, leadership, and partners, managing competing priorities while driving consensus and delivery.
<ul>
<li>
Passion for building impactful digital products - Strong interest in shaping meaningful digital experiences that improve the daily interactions of residents and businesses.
<li>
Strong product management experience - At least 3+ years of experience managing digital products, with a proven track record of delivering measurable outcomes and value
<li>

Technical fluency in modern digital practices - Familiarity with technologies and practices such as Agile methodologies, CI/CD, cloud-native architectures, RESTful APIs, and modern authentication frameworks (e.g., OAuth 2.0).
<li>
Experience in rapid prototyping and AI-enabled development - Hands-on experience leveraging AI-assisted tools (e.g., vibe coding) to quickly prototype, validate, and iterate product ideas.
<li>

Knowledge of digital ecosystem concepts - Understanding of areas such as digital identity (including self-sovereign identity), data privacy and protection, and platform or two-sided marketplace models.
<li>
Strong analytical and data-driven mindset - Ability to derive insights from data, translate them into actionable decisions, and measure product success through clear metrics.
<li>
Ability to navigate ambiguity and complexity - Comfortable operating in uncertain environments, with the ability to simplify complex concepts and communicate them clearly to diverse stakeholders.
<li>
Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills - Proven ability to collaborate across organisational boundaries and influence without direct authority.
<li>
Demonstrated leadership in cross-functional teams - Experience leading and aligning multidisciplinary teams (engineering, design, business) to deliver high-quality products.
<li>
Domain expertise (preferred) - Familiarity with welfare campaigns, grant management, or public sector programmes would be an advantage.

About the product
Singapore Customs is a regulatory agency under the Ministry of Finance, with the mission of protecting revenue and facilitating trade for a thriving Singapore economy.

Customs eServices serves as Customs' Single Digital Touchpoint for 6,500 Singapore based Companies, offering trade facilitation services including Hand-Carried Export Scheme, Permit Clearance Enquiry Service, Permit Returns, and eGuarantee@Gov. eGuarantee@Gov which started as service meant for Customs, had scaled to support more than 220 school, agencies and financial institutions. This enterprise-wide platform standardizes user experience design, and reusable components (e.g. SPCP integration, SSO, Call-to-Actions, Notifications, Payments, Fileshare) while expanding its compliance service portfolio to enhance revenue protection, such as eLOA and VDP. Customs eServices handled about 2.5 million domestic transactions annually.
Beyond serving the domestic market, Customs eServices enhances Singapore's competitive advantage through digital exchange of customs certificates with trading partners, accelerating cross-border trade facilitation and tariff processing compared to non-digitally connected hubs. Customs eServices handled about 200,000 cross border transactions annually.
To support Customs to meet its 2030 transformation goals, the product teams continue to upgrade existing and rollout new capabilities for trade and compliance. Behind the scenes of some of these eServices are the Customs officers who process the cases or correspond with their respective target market segments. Hence, we are looking for a passionate Product Manager to join the Customs eServices team and work together with the business teams to meet the demands for the benefit of Customs and companies.

What the Role Is

The Government Technology Agency (GovTech) is the lead agency driving Singapore's Smart Nation initiatives and public sector digital transformation. At GovTech, we offer you a purposeful career to make lives better.

SHIP-HATS is the CI/CD backbone of the Singapore Government Tech Stack. It is a platform product, the common secure foundation that government engineering teams rely on to build, test, and ship software. Over 670 government systems are onboarded on SHIP-HATS, with more than 21,000 deployments every month, a 4.76 out of 5 satisfaction score, and 99.95% uptime. The decisions made here do not just affect one product or one team. They shape how the Singapore Government builds software.

The primary users of SHIP-HATS are developers and DevOps engineers across government agencies. The key decision makers you will engage are engineering leads and agency IT teams who determine how their teams build and ship software. This is a large and complex product with many stakeholders, and success requires working closely with colleagues across engineering, operations, policy, and the Product Ops team.

We are seeking a Senior Product Manager to take full ownership of SHIP-HATS, operates with a high degree of autonomy, and is not afraid to challenge the status quo when the platform needs to evolve. You will report to the Product and Policy Lead.
What You Will Be Working On
Platform Strategy and Roadmap

You will own the product roadmap for SHIP-HATS, making prioritisation decisions across a complex platform that serves hundreds of government systems. You will define success metrics, measure them at least quarterly, and use data to drive decisions and hold yourself accountable for outcomes. Platform thinking is central: you are ensuring the platform is reliable, extensible, and enabling teams to build on it with confidence.
AI-Native Developer Experience

You will own the product vision for how SHIP-HATS evolves to support an AI-native software development lifecycle, working closely with the AI PM team. This means ensuring the platform's toolchain, including pipelines, code review workflows, and security scanning, is ready for how developers will increasingly work with AI.
Adoption and User Insight

Your primary users are developers and DevOps engineers. You will work closely with the Product Ops Specialist to track how SHIP-HATS is being adopted across government agencies, from basic CI/CD usage to more advanced DevSecOps practices. You will synthesise adoption signals and user feedback into clear product recommendations, and ensure the platform meets agencies where they are while helping them raise their practices over time.
Cross-Team Collaboration and Vendor Management

SHIP-HATS is a large product with many moving parts. You will work closely with colleagues across engineering, operations, policy, and the Product Ops team to deliver on the platform roadmap. You will also manage relationships with key tool vendors in the SHIP-HATS ecosystem, staying close to their roadmaps, negotiating on features and pricing, and ensuring the programme gets strategic value from each partnership.
What Success Looks Like
<ul>
<li>
SHIP-HATS has clear success metrics that are tracked regularly and being acted on.
<li>
The platform is evolving to support AI-native developer workflows, with a clear roadmap for how SHIP-HATS enables AI adoption.
<li>
Adoption is growing across government agencies, with teams moving from basic usage toward more advanced DevSecOps practices.
<li>
Key vendor partnerships are well-managed and deliver strategic value to the programme.
What We Are Looking For / What You Bring

The AI Programme builds shared AI infrastructure that agencies can run in production, instead of rebuilding the same foundations independently. It sits within Government Digital Products, and it owns a small number of central products that a lot of other people's work now depends on.

Three of them shape the job. There's the agent surface public officers use to get through the day: it reaches into their mail, their documents and their case systems, so it has to be quick, honest about what it just did on their behalf, and safe to point at real records. Underneath sits the developer platform, where teams across government bring their own agents, MCP servers and skills and move them into production through review, approval and audit. And there's the model and capability layer that most agencies meet first: a compliant gateway to multiple production-approved models behind an OpenAI-compatible API, alongside shared speech, vision and document capabilities (live transcription, image and video classification, key information extraction) that every agency would otherwise go and procure separately, with guardrails, quotas and cost attribution already attached.

Building an agent demo is easy now, and that's fine, because it means the hard parts have moved. Most of what we work on lives after the demo. An agent decides to call a tool that sends an email on someone's behalf, and the approval gate for that has to be enforced by the runtime, not requested politely in a system prompt. A tool loop needs a stop condition that doesn't depend on the model deciding it's done. Token spend has to trace back to the team that caused it, and when an agency's agent gets slower this week, someone has to be able to say why. Rollback gets interesting when the artefact is a prompt, a tool schema and a model version rather than a binary. Very little of that is model work. It's orchestration, platform and operations, which is roughly the job.
You'll work across all of it: the surfaces officers see, the runtime underneath, the platform other engineers build on, and the unglamorous business of keeping the whole thing up. Your user is a public officer with something to finish today. Your customer is often another engineering team in another agency.
What you'll do
<ul>
<li>
Build and run the surfaces officers use daily. Streaming, approval interrupts, resumable sessions, and interfaces that stay readable when an agent is doing four things at once
<li>
Build the runtime beneath them: tool orchestration, approval gates enforced in code, loop limits, per-turn tool filtering, memory and checkpointing, model routing and fallback
<li>

Work on the platform half, where the job is to let other teams onboard their own agents, MCP servers, skills and models, with the policy checks and promotion workflows that let them move to production safely and repeatedly
<li>
Extend the shared capability APIs (speech, vision, document extraction) and keep them fast and cheap enough that agencies reach for them instead of building their own
<li>
Integrate with what government already runs: identity, mail and calendar, document stores, agency line-of-business systems, the existing CI/CD pipelines
<li>
Instrument the things you'll want to argue about later. Tool call traces, latency, error taxonomies, cost per team and per feature
<li>
Build evaluation into delivery, so changing a prompt, a tool or a model becomes a measurable decision instead of an argument
<li>
Run it. Deployments, incidents, capacity, cost, and the support queue of officers who found the case nobody thought of
<li>
Work with agency teams as users and as builders, and turn the third bespoke request into a platform feature
<li>
Take part in security and privacy reviews on the assumption that these systems get audited, because they do
You'll thrive here if
<ul>
<li>
You want the thing you wrote to be used by someone doing real work the next morning
<li>
You're interested in what happens after launch, not only up to it
<li>
The constraints (classification, audit trails, approvals, cost accountability) read to you as design problems rather than obstacles to route around
<li>
You have a view on what belongs in a prompt and what belongs in the backend, and you'll defend it
<li>
You'd rather ship something narrow and run it properly than demo something broad
<li>
You use agentic coding tools every day and have opinions about where they help and where they quietly cost you
<li>
You can talk to a policy officer in the morning and debug a streaming protocol after lunch
<li>
You expect the model layer to change under you every few months, and you design so that's survivable
We're deliberately open on background. This is a broad role, and the strongest signal is something you built, shipped and then had to keep running, not a number of years.
<ul>
<li>
Strong engineering fundamentals and fluency in TypeScript or Python (we mostly write React and Node on the front, Python and Node behind it, Postgres, AWS)
<li>
Comfort moving across frontend, backend, data and cloud rather than settling into one layer
<li>
Something you've taken end to end: designed it, built it, deployed it, watched it break, fixed it
<li>
Working knowledge of containers, CI/CD and infrastructure as code (Terraform or similar), or the appetite to pick them up quickly
<li>
Understanding of authentication, authorisation and careful data handling, which matter more than usual when an agent is the one holding the credentials
<li>
Practical experience with LLM APIs, tool calling, retrieval or agentic workflows is welcome. Strong engineering and real curiosity will beat an AI-heavy CV with nothing shipped behind it
<li>
Fluency with agentic development tools such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor
<li>
Writing you'd be happy to put in front of someone who will never read the code
<li>
Reliability with data that belongs to the public

Useful, but genuinely not expected: evaluation harnesses for AI systems, MCP server authoring, streaming protocols (SSE, WebSockets), managed agent runtimes on AWS or GCP, Kubernetes, observability stacks, or any prior public sector work.
If you've built one substantial thing you're proud of and can walk us through the decisions inside it, we'd like to talk. You don't need to have worked on AI systems before.

Users from the first week, across agencies with genuinely different needs and maturity
<li>
An unusual split, where you build the platform and also build on it, so you live with your own abstractions
<li>
Ownership from design through operations, and the autonomy that has to come with it
<li>
Work on production problems in agent systems: tool orchestration, governance, memory, evaluation and cost control under real audit and reliability constraints
<li>
Colleagues across GovTech's AI Practice, Government Technology Office and product teams, and a mandate broad enough that good work travels
<li>
Support to stay hands-on: learning budget, conferences, and time to go deep on the parts of this that nobody has settled yet

FileSG is a central, secure file management system designed to streamline the issuance and distribution of official documents to Singapore residents. We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join our team. In this role, you will take ownership of complex, cross-cutting technical work while actively raising the bar for those around you. You will be expected to operate with a high degree of independence — making sound architectural decisions, leading incident response, and delivering features that span multiple services or systems — while also investing meaningfully in the growth of junior software engineers and the health of the team.

This is a role for someone who is equally comfortable writing a technical design document, reviewing a colleague's code for AI-introduced antipatterns, and facilitating alignment between engineers and stakeholders on a tricky design trade-off.
Craft & Technical Execution
<ul>

• You will design and deliver moderately complex features that span multiple components or services, with genuine attention to modularity, scalability, and resiliency. This means evaluating solution options, sharing well-reasoned recommendations, and proactively addressing technical debt before it compounds.

• On quality and DevOps, you will contribute to reusable test automation frameworks and help the team adopt better observability, CI/CD, and automation practices. You will ensure that features you own are properly monitored and that issues surface early rather than in production.

• You will build deep knowledge of your team's product architecture, dependencies, and data flows, and use that knowledge to make independent technical decisions and author design documents with minimal guidance. You will also conduct architecture reviews for junior engineers' work, offering constructive and actionable feedback.
• When incidents occur, you will lead triage and debugging within your domain, contribute root cause analyses, and drive concrete preventive actions through post-incident reviews.

• Security, compliance, and performance are design constraints in your work, not afterthoughts. You will apply the organisation's recommended platforms and tools effectively, and escalate deviations appropriately.

• You will also play a key role in how the team works with AI-assisted development — writing clear, unambiguous technical specifications that serve as effective context for both AI tools and junior engineers, identifying when AI-generated code introduces technical debt or security risks, and establishing team-level norms for reviewing AI-generated output before it merges.
Ownership & Delivery
<ul>
• You will take full end-to-end ownership of broad project scopes, navigating uncertainty and ensuring successful outcomes.
• You are comfortable taking calculated risks and learning openly from both successes and failures.
• You actively mentor junior team members — sharing knowledge, breaking down problems, and providing constructive feedback that raises overall team productivity.
Strategic Contribution
<ul>
• You will translate team goals into actionable plans, breaking down and prioritising work and contributing to project strategy.
• You proactively identify opportunities, drive workstreams, and synthesise data into clear recommendations that connect to organisational impact.
• At the project level, you anticipate risks and put mitigations in place before they become blockers.
Culture & Organisational Influence
<ul>
• You will coordinate cross-functional collaboration and help ensure projects are delivered effectively across team boundaries.
• You navigate disagreements constructively, facilitating alignment among team members and stakeholders.

• You challenge existing processes where improvement is warranted and drive change initiatives at the team or division level. You share learnings openly — both wins and failures — and make recommendations that help the team continuously improve.
People Management
<ul>

• This role includes a developmental people management component. With close guidance from your software engineering manager, you will support team coordination by communicating project goals and priorities clearly, and helping team members understand how their individual work connects to broader objectives.

• You will conduct regular check-ins with one or two direct or indirect reports, focusing on work progress and basic feedback delivery, and help team members work through day-to-day blockers with technical mentoring.
• You will also participate in recruitment activities where applicable.
Please note that this will be a 2-year fixed term contract.

GovTech’s Culture, Community and Youth Cluster (CCYC) partners with the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) and its statutory boards — including the National Arts Council, People’s Association, Sport Singapore, and MUIS — to deliver digital products that strengthen community life across Singapore. Singaporeans across community engagement, cultural participation, youth development, and sports and active lifestyle.
This role sits within CCYC and will be working on MUIS products, specifically Muslim.SG.

MUIS (Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura) is the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore, the statutory body that looks after the interests of Singapore’s Muslim community. Muslim.SG is its Muslim lifestyle platform — available as a website and on iOS and Android — that aims to inspire and empower Singaporeans through Islamic religious content.

Who We Are Looking For
We are looking for a Senior UX Designer to own the end-to-end design of Muslim.SG — across the web portal and both mobile platforms — from discovery through to launch and continuous improvement.

This is a full product design role. You will conduct research, shape product direction, design the interface, and stay close to whether your work is actually landing with users. You will be the design voice your squad relies on, and the person accountable for the experience quality
of a platform that serves Singapore’s Muslim community every day.

You bring strong craft, clear product thinking, and the ability to navigate the particular design considerations of Muslim.SG — a platform where content is religiously and culturally significant, users span a wide range of digital literacy, and the relationship between the product and its community requires care and sensitivity.
[What you will be working on]

Own the Full Design Arc
Lead design from 0 to 1 to 100 across the Muslim.SG web and mobile products. This means shaping initial concepts, designing and shipping the first version of features, and continuously improving the experience based on data, user feedback, and evolving community needs. You stay accountable to the outcome — you do not hand off and move on.

Design Across Web and Mobile
Muslim.SG lives across three surfaces: a web portal and native apps on iOS and Android. You will maintain design coherence and quality across all three, understanding where the experiences should diverge — in navigation patterns, interaction models, and platform conventions — and where they must converge, in content hierarchy, information presentation, and community tone.

Conduct Continuous, Embedded Research
Run user interviews, usability tests, and contextual checks as a regular part of your workflow— not as a separate phase. Muslim.SG’s user base is genuinely diverse: different levels of digital confidence, different levels of religious literacy, different languages. You stay close to that reality and let it shape your design decisions rather than designing from assumptions.

Drive Product Thinking Through Design
Bring a product mindset to every design decision. Think about retention, activation, and adoption alongside usability. Use design as a lever for impact: improving onboarding, reducing friction in high-drop-off moments, and creating experiences that make the platform feel valuable enough to return to — especially for users who are developing their own digital habits.

Maintain and Evolve the Design System
Take ownership of the Muslim.SG design system across web and mobile. Keep components consistent, well-documented, and scalable as the platform grows. You balance system rigour with the pragmatism needed to move at product pace.

Work directly with MUIS stakeholders — community officers, religious officers, operations teams — as well as internal product and engineering partners. Present your work clearly. Advocate for the user. Navigate competing priorities without losing design integrity. When you disagree, you say so with evidence, not volume.

Contribute to Design Culture
As a senior IC, you help set the quality bar. You give constructive feedback, share what you know, and contribute to shared design practices within CCYC. The standard of work you produce, and how you work, shapes what the team collectively considers good.

You will contribute to the development of one or more of our four strategic technical initiatives:

Standardised Data Platform
<ul>
• Build and maintain unified data platform infrastructure for government agencies
• Develop APIs and services that standardise data ingestion, processing, and storage
• Create reusable components and templates for agency data platform implementation

Unified Frontend / DataHive
<ul>

• Implement request management workflows and approval systems

Unified Serving Backbone
<ul>
• Design and implement standardised data delivery APIs and microservices
• Build robust data serving infrastructure that can handle high-volume requests
• Develop authentication and authorisation systems for secure data access
• Create monitoring and alerting systems for data delivery pipelines
Observability & Governance Infrastructure
<ul>
• Build central observability systems for data quality monitoring and lineage tracking
• Develop dashboards and analytics tools for data usage patterns
• Implement automated data quality checks and validation frameworks
• Create audit trails and compliance reporting systems

<ul>
• Build end-to-end data analytics products/platforms with your team
• Design system architectures
• Write production quality code
• Manage deployments to cloud and (occasionally) on-premise infrastructure
• Build prototypes to demonstrate technology opportunities
• Learn and share knowledge in a multi-disciplinary team
• Establish best practices
• Share your expertise and mentor other engineers
• Help with recruiting.

We build products that serve a variety of agency users, who use them to solve highly meaningful problems pertinent to our society, from transportation, to education, to healthcare. The public sector is full of opportunities where even the simplest software can have a big impact on people’s lives. We are here to improve how we live as a society through what we can offer as a government.
<ul>
<li>

Rapid Prototyping - Instead of spending too much time debating ideas we prefer testing them. This identifies potential problems quickly, and more importantly, conveys what is possible to others easily.
<li>
Reliable Productization - To scale an idea, a prototype or a Minimum Viable Product to a software product, we scrutinize and commit to its usability, reliability, scalability and maintainability.
<li>

Ownership - In addition to technical responsibilities, this means having ideas on how things should be done and taking responsibility for seeing them through. Building something that you believe in is the best way to build something good.
<li>

Continuous Learning - Working on new ideas often means not fully understanding what you are working on. Taking time to learn new architectures, frameworks, technologies, and even languages is not just encouraged but essential.

The customers for our products are normally agency users, which means that breadth of knowledge in government IT infrastructure and experience in government networks will help. Since our direction is cloud-first, you will likely have some experience in patch/update scheduling, and knowledge of security incident response procedures. A disciplined approach and strong problem-solving instincts are fundamental to succeed. Your aptitude for completing the tasks and attitude to continuous learning are more valued than any formal certification. To succeed, you will need to possess some of the following:
<ul>
<li>
Excellent problem solving and methodical troubleshooting skills
<li>
Strong knowledge and experience in DevOps automation, containerization and orchestration using tools eg. Ansible, Airflow, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, Artifactory/Nexus Sonatype
<li>
Cloud computing deployment and management experience in AWS, GCP
<li>
Strong scripting skills e.g. Python, Bash, JavaScript, Scala, Rust, Go
<li>
Strong understanding of Apache Spark/Flink, Hadoop, distributed file systems and resource scaling/scheduling, streaming message queues (RabbitMQ, Kafka)
<li>
Strong understanding of virtualization and networking concepts
<li>
Experience with patch maintenance, regression testing and security incident response
<li>
Experience with interactive workloads, machine learning toolkits and how they integrate with cloud computing e.g. Databricks, KX
<li>
Experience with highly scalable distributed systems
<li>
Experience with on-premise deployments, government application and networking infrastructure/routing
<li>
Breadth of knowledge - OS, networking, distributed computing, cloud computing

[About the Team]
The Ministry of Education is building AI products and shared platform capabilities that can improve how students learn, how teachers work, and how HQ teams run complex operational workflows.

The AI Platform & Capability Programme sits at the centre of this work. We build and support AI-native products such as learning assistants, marking tools, procurement agents, multimodal prototypes, and the shared evaluation, observability, model-access, and governance capabilities needed to scale them responsibly.

We are hiring software engineers who can take ambiguous problems from brief to production. This is not a pure research role and not a demo-building role. The work is to build reliable, maintainable, policy-sensitive AI systems that can survive real users, real operational constraints, and public-sector trust requirements.

AI will support how we build. Engineers still own the design, judgement, quality, and consequences of what ships.

How we build

We prefer simple, durable engineering choices over novelty for its own sake. The stack may vary by product, but the principles do not: clear architecture, automated testing, CI/CD, observability, secure-by-design delivery, and systems that are easy to reason about after launch.

The team’s operating model is product-led and platform-amplified. Product squads prove value in real education or HQ workflows; shared platform capabilities make those products observable, testable, governable, and reusable across MOE. Engineers may work inside a product squad, on the shared AI platform, or in a forward-deployed model where they help a vertical team build AI capability before bringing reusable patterns back to the centre
<ul>
• Design, build, test, deploy, and operate AI-enabled products and platform components across MOE.
• Work on areas such as LLM integration, agentic workflows, evaluation harnesses, observability, guardrails, model access, retrieval/memory patterns, and multimodal AI use cases.
• Take ambiguous education or corporate operations problems and turn them into maintainable software with clear success metrics.
• Build production features for products such as procurement automation, teacher-facing AI tools, learning assistants, and evaluation/monitoring platforms.
• Create engineering patterns that other product teams can reuse, including templates, playbooks, test harnesses, and reference implementations.
• Work closely with product managers, designers, data scientists, governance colleagues, and business owners.
• Use AI coding and development tools to accelerate delivery while retaining human accountability for design and quality.
• Participate in design reviews, code reviews, incident response, and technical decision-making.
• Push for root-cause fixes rather than surface-level patches.
<ul>
• Strong software engineering fundamentals: system design, testing, version control, CI/CD, observability, security, and maintainable code.
• Good engineering judgement: you can explain trade-offs clearly and defend a technical position without becoming attached to it.
• Comfort with ambiguity: you can move from unclear policy, education, or operational needs into a working product shape.
• Appetite for AI-native engineering: LLM applications, evaluation, agentic workflows, RAG/memory, multimodal models, or AI-assisted development.
• Pragmatic taste in technology: you choose boring, durable tools when they are right, and newer AI tooling only when it genuinely improves the system.
• Ownership mindset: you do not stop at prototype handoff; you care about deployment, monitoring, user feedback, and maintainability.
• Ability to work with non-technical stakeholders in sensitive public-sector domains.
• Bias for measurable quality: you care about evals, regression checks, traceability, and evidence before scaling.
Nice to have
<ul>
• Experience building production LLM or AI-enabled applications.
• Experience with evaluation frameworks, prompt/context engineering, model monitoring, Langfuse/OpenTelemetry-style tracing, or AI safety guardrails.
• Experience with Python, TypeScript, Go, PostgreSQL, containerised deployment, cloud services, or government/cloud-restricted environments.
• Experience building internal platforms, developer tooling, or reusable engineering kits.
• Familiarity with education, public-sector operations, procurement, or high-trust digital services.
What success looks like

In the first 6 months, you should have shipped meaningful production work in at least one product or platform area, improved the team’s engineering quality bar, and helped convert one-off AI delivery into reusable capability. The best engineers in this role will not just “build features”; they will help define how MOE builds, evaluates, governs, and scales AI products.
Why this role matters

MOE’s AI work is moving beyond experiments. The next challenge is to make AI useful, safe, measurable, and maintainable across real education and HQ workflows. This role is for engineers who want to build public-good AI systems with national-scale relevance, while shaping the operating model for how product teams use AI responsibly.

As a Software Engineer, you will take on meaningful ownership of features and technical work that spans multiple components of our products. You will work with a degree of independence while continuing to grow through mentorship, and you will play an active role in shaping the quality, reliability, and culture of the team you work in.
Craft & Execution

You will deliver features and proofs of concept that span multiple components or modules, typically working across two to three areas within your team. While you will receive mentorship on architectural decisions and cross-component integration, you are expected to make thoughtful trade-offs between performance, security, and maintainability based on your understanding of the context. You will write and review code with clarity and long-term maintainability in mind, applying good engineering practices consistently, and you will expand test coverage — including unit and integration tests — to support key workflows and reduce flakiness.

Beyond feature delivery, you will address pockets of technical debt within your domain, suggest improvements that enhance product performance or team velocity, and contribute to CI/CD processes and deployment pipelines. You will also take a deliberate approach to balancing short-term delivery speed with long-term code health, flagging when quick fixes introduce future risk, and applying organisational platform and compliance standards effectively.

After your work ships, you are expected to follow through on its impact — checking metrics, reviewing error rates, and addressing post-deployment issues proactively. You will actively participate in incident triage and resolution with team support, and escalate complex issues when needed.

You will also bring rigour to the use of AI-generated code, reviewing it for correctness, edge cases, security issues, and maintainability to the same standard as any human-authored contribution. Writing clear task descriptions and specifications to get higher-quality AI assistance and reduce rework is part of how you work.
Ownership

You will independently own your assigned tasks and projects, identifying and addressing issues proactively with minimal guidance. You will know when to seek help and from whom, and you will look for opportunities to recommend improvements to processes or outcomes within your own work.
Strategic Alignment

You will align your work with your team's goals and priorities, focusing on tasks that deliver the most expected business value. You will adapt to changing priorities independently, without needing to be redirected.
Culture and Organisational Influence

You will collaborate with peers and stakeholders to ensure work is executed effectively, address minor conflicts constructively and respectfully, and suggest improvements that enhance team effectiveness. You will share knowledge, resources, successes, and failures openly — because you understand that team success depends on everyone having the information they need.
<ul>
• Have a demonstrated ability to build software - Prior work and personal projects count for much more than specific degrees.
• Write code to solve abstract programming problems - Clear thinking, the ability to debug, and understanding the limits of an approach matter much more than getting the “correct” answer.
• Talk and reason about code with other engineers - We work as a team, so you need to be able to not just solve problems, but have other people understand your solutions.
• Take initiative to make things happen - Our job is to push for change in government, so we need to challenge the status quo and not wait for instruction.

• Want to work for the public good - We are public servants; we serve the public. This sometimes means ignoring political pressures and misguided policies. We need people who will push back if something is not in public interest.
Overall, we look for people who have ability, initiative, good communication, and strong values.
Please note that this will be a 2-year fixed term contract.

How do we work
Job overview
We have built a scrum team of technologists who have developed digital products to improve citizen's experience of using the agency's e-services.

You have understood the overall product strategy, did a stock take on the UX status of the project, and contributed design screens for concurrent active sprints.

You should have run an inception, gathered requirements, co-create with stakeholders and scrum team, tested, prototyped, and shipped at least one new feature to the product backlog.

You will have led research efforts to identify at least one opportunity for the product to grow or proposed enhancements for the existing tracks, in collaboration with designers, engineers, and product managers.

You will continue to solve problems such as:

<ul>

You are collaborative and understand that co-creating a product with the team

<li>

<li>

You are meticulous and possess good problem solving skills
<li>
Frontend development knowledge is a bonus
